News.title: Spain v Argentina LIVE: Ugly scenes after full time as Spain win second World Cup in their history
News.content:
Spain lift World Cup 2026 trophy after defeating Argentina

Spain won the World Cup for the second time in their history as they claimed a 1-0 extra-time victory over 10-man Argentina before ugly scenes on the pitch after full time marred the celebrations.

Ferran Torres’ smashed finish in the 106th minute was enough for Spain to add to their 2010 triumph but Argentina – who offered little throughout the match – reacted badly after the final whistle, with players brawling, Leandro Paredes sent off after grabbing Eric Garcia by the throat and reports of punches being thrown.

Donald Trump then unsurprisingly inserted himself into things post-match as he lurked towards the edge of Spain’s trophy lift to ensure he was in the photo, despite Gianni Infantino trying to usher him away, after presenting the Spanish players with medals and the trophy. However, the US president was audibly booed when he first walked on to the pitch with Infantino.

After a dire spectacle for 90 minutes, with neither side mustering any real chances, Enzo Fernandez stupidly got himself sent off just before the end of normal time when he crunched Pau Cubarsi on halfway and was deservedly shown a second yellow card, having earlier been booked for dissent.

Spain then finally made the breakthrough when Torres calmly hammered home at the start of the second half of extra time and it meant Lionel Messi was denied on surely his final World Cup appearance, with the aftermath further souring the occasion for the 39-year-old football icon.

Relive all the action from the World Cup final, below

News.title: Argentina’s World Cup final performance was a disgrace to Lionel Messi’s legacy
News.content:

Don’t cry for them, Argentina. Some tears were shed by Lionel Messi, after an unsatisfactory end to one of the great World Cup careers. But his team-mates merit rather less sympathy. What had been a valiant, dramatic and compelling attempt to retain the World Cup ended with a lack of discipline, creativity and, above all, shots.

The historic feat, it transpired, was not becoming the first team since Brazil in 1962 to win consecutive World Cups, but in being officially the least attacking team ever in a final. Argentina had no shot of any kind in 90 minutes, an xG of 0.00 when it went to extra time. Spain had 20 shots before Argentina’s first, in the 121st minute.

All this with a man who has been involved in more World Cup goals than anyone else, who many believe is the greatest footballer ever. A team with Messi should not be this dull, this focused on delaying and disrupting.

open image in gallery Argentina offered nothing in the final and Messi was left anonymous ( Reuters )

But after Fifa wasted everyone’s time getting into the MetLife Stadium, Argentina wasted their time inside it. If anything can be savoured from their exercise in nothingness, it is the thought they may have bored Donald Trump and the battalion of celebrities who somehow acquired tickets that could have gone to actual supporters.

The many actors among them may have been bemused: this was a supposed blockbuster that was often lacking in drama, where the eventual starring role was assumed by Ferran Torres, a minor character who did not figure in the first hour. Messi, the man with top billing, endured an uncharacteristic descent into anonymity.

His eventual tally stands at three World Cup finals; one won, two 1-0 defeats. For six weeks, the improbable had come to feel possible: that, at 39, he could create the 2022 final, when scored two goals and lifted the trophy. This World Cup had felt a continuation of the last for Messi: when he scored in the first five games, took Miroslav Klose’s all-time scoring record, closed in on the Golden Boot. In a country where many spend fortunes trying to prevent the ageing process – perhaps some of Fifa’s famous guests among them – Messi seemed to have found a method that involved nothing more than footballing talent.

But this was a first game this World Cup he has not really influenced. He scored in the first five, stirred late on against Switzerland, made both goals against England. Julian Alvarez, a forward who may command a £150m fee, ended up on the left of midfield before he was substituted.

open image in gallery Messi will be 43 by the time the next World Cup comes around and he was given no support against Spain ( Getty )

And Argentina’s lack of ambition was staggering. Perhaps their capacity for late goals convinced them they did not need to try and score early on. And yet it was only Torres’ belated strike that brought them to life. Part of it could be attributed to Spain’s watertight defence, but only part. It underlined that, until now, a team with a lack of pace or width had prospered because largely because of an over-reliance on Messi.

As he was starved of service, Argentinian resorted to anti-futbol. They have often showed the best side of their footballing traditions in this tournament. In the biggest game, they doubled down on their worst instincts.

As finals involving Argentina go, this was more 1990 than 2022, 1986 or 1978. Enzo Fernandez’s deserved dismissal may have highlighted his stupidity in getting booked for dissent. When he sent Pau Cubarsi flying, however, he may have been fortunate only to get a second yellow card. The third Argentinian to be sent off in a World Cup final was reluctant to leave the pitch. Perhaps Argentina had got away with enough skulduggery of late that Fernandez believed he was immune to such a sanction.

Fifa may yet need to take action against another Argentinian. Leandro Paredes was summoned at half-time. Argentina’s resident prince of darkness was soon in the book for an off-the-ball barge on Rodri. After the final whistle, he threw Gavi to the ground; perhaps a punch or two, as well.

open image in gallery Leandro Paredes was involved in ugly clashes with Eric Garcia and Gavi at full time ( Reuters )

open image in gallery Ezno Fernandez sent Pau Cubarsi flying after getting a stupid yellow card for dissent ( Getty )

After Fernandez’s red card, Argentina’s task became tougher. In their defence of the trophy, defence became the operative word. Emi Martinez was increasingly busy; increasingly impressive, too, with a fine save from Lamine Yamal’s free kick and a still better one from Nico Williams’ header.

But over 120 minutes, it became harder to believe this side had won one World Cup and two Copa Americas. They were outclassed and out-passed by Spain, arguably the first top-class team they have met en route. When the draw was made, they could have been pitted against Portugal in the last eight and Brazil in the last four. They got neither. They still almost stumbled at every hurdle. They conjured dramatic finishes in four knockout rounds, but they required them, too.

At the last, they tarnished memories of those victories and their glory days. Argentina were unedifying and unthreatening. But a signature song of one of New Jersey’s favourite musical sons, Frank Sinatra, had been played before kick-off and ultimately Argentina did it their way.

Argentina centre-back Cristian Romero snubbed Donald Trump’s handshake during the presentation of the runners-up medals at the 2026 World Cup final.

Argentina lost 1-0 after extra time to Spain in a largely dire final at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, as Ferran Torres smashed home a 106th-minute winner to give La Roja a second World Cup triumph in their history – following their 2010 success.

open image in gallery Cristian Romero snubbed Donald Trump for a handshake during the medal presentation ( Screenshot / BBC )

Romero started the match at the heart of the Argentine defence, alongside Lisandro Martinez, but was subbed off at the 70-minute mark with what appeared to be some sort of injury. His centre-back partner Martinez had himself come off injured towards the end of the first half.

However, the 28-year-old Tottenham defender still made his mark after that as he snubbed a handshake from Trump when the US president was conducting the medal presentation.

Trump was handing out medals to both teams, as well the individual tournament awards, and Romero shook the hand of both Fifa president Gianni Infantino and Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum, who were either side of Trump, but did not engage with the US president.

Last summer, Trump made headlines when Chelsea won the Fifa Club World Cup in the same stadium, as he joined Blues captain Reece James at the heart of the celebrations to lift the trophy.

This time, after presenting the trophy to Spain, Trump moved towards the edge of the group for the initial lift, ensuring he would be in the photo, before Infantino subtly tried to move him away from the scene.

The reaction to the president in New Jersey on Sunday night was audibly negative with boos heard around the stadium.

open image in gallery Trump hung around long enough to ensure he was in the torphy lift photo ( Getty )

Trump walked out onto the pitch alongside Infantino to loud jeers and whistle before shaking hands with numerous guests, including Governor of Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia and Newcastle chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan. The ambient crowd noise in the stadium was about 78 decibels and the booing brought it to 84.

Romero was part of the Argentina side that won the World Cup in Qatar four years ago but they failed to retain their crown this time around, with an insipid display in the final ultimately costing them.

At least one American service member was killed after the controlled detonation of an unexploded Iranian drone, according to U.S. Central Command.

A second service member was wounded during Saturday’s operation, military officials announced Sunday.

The U.S. military also recovered unidentified remains after a search for a missing service member in the wake of an earlier attack that killed two other service members on Friday. Those remains are believed to be those of a third service member killed in the strike.

Sunday’s announcement brings the U.S. death toll from the months-long war in Iran to at least 17 service members. More than 400 troops have been wounded throughout the campaign.

A tenuous ceasefire has effectively collapsed, risking an all-out assault and a revival of the months-long war. American forces launched a ninth consecutive night of strikes on Sunday as Iran ramps up missile and drone attacks on U.S. allies and assets in the Persian Gulf.

open image in gallery A munition launched from an American warship during an eighth consecutive strikes on Iran. At least three US service members have died during a week of attacks ( Reuters )

“Iran has been very, very badly damaged,” President Donald Trump told reporters Sunday evening.

“We hit them very hard again tonight, and we did that in honor of the probably three — it’s probably three, as opposed to two — great patriots,” he added.

The Trump administration mounted a new wave of strikes earlier this month after accusing Iran of attacking merchant ships in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran then launched attacks at Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Syria and Jordan, warning of a “full-scale offensive” should U.S. attacks continue.

U.S. deaths include six service members who were killed after two refueling jets collided above Iraq earlier this year. An Iranian drone strike that hit a command post in Kuwait killed another six service members.

A Navy pilot died in a helicopter crash in the Arabian Sea earlier this month.

Trump, who was golfing at his Bedminster, New Jersey club on Saturday as Central Command announced the initial deaths, said news of Friday’s incident is a “very sad thing.”

“We hate to see it happen. It’s in service to our country,” he told News Nation.

open image in gallery Donald Trump arrived at the World Cup final at MetLife stadium shortly after US military officials announced the death of a third service member amid the ongoing war in Iran ( Getty )

A statement issued on behalf of Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei said Trump’s signature on a memorandum of understanding was “worthless and invalid” and accused the U.S. of repeatedly breaching the commitments of the temporary peace deal.

He warned “unforgettable lessons” should U.S. strikes continue.

Trump told NewsNation on Saturday that he “couldn’t care less” about Iran abandoning the bilateral memorandum that was reached a month earlier.

“Godspeed, heroes,” Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth wrote in a statement on X in response to news of the two service members on Saturday.

“Their sacrifice only stiffens our resolve,” he added.

Spain are world champions after a dominant win over Argentina in the final of the 2026 World Cup, with Ferran Torres giving La Roja a famous win in New Jersey.

Both sides played out a scrappy first half, and though Spain were dominant as they stifled the holders, neither side could fashion a clear-cut chance, save for one early effort from Lamine Yamal that was blocked by Lisandro Martinez.

The second half played out in similar fashion, with Argentina failing to have a shot in 90 minutes before Enzo Fernandez changed the game, the midfielder sent off for a poor challenge on Pau Cubarsi as he earned two yellow cards in around 10 minutes.

It left Argentina with a mountain to climb in extra time as they looked to fight back against Spain’s dominance, and eventually the advantage told, with Torres opening the scoring after a clever header from Nico Williams.

In the end, it was enough for Spain to secure a win that was far more dominant than the scoreline suggests, with Luis de la Fuente producing a managerial masterclass to give La Roja their second World Cup triumph.

Here’s how the players rated in the World Cup final:

Spain

Unai Simon, 6: The Spain keeper was alert early on to stop Messi going clean through, but that was almost the only thing he had to do all game as Argentina failed to have a shot before 90 minutes.

Pedro Porro, 7: The Tottenham man defended well when called upon, notably when shepherding Gonzalez off the ball after a promising opening for Argentina. He was always willing to join the attack and provided another outlet to help Spain dominate possession, and it was his cross that led to Torres’ goal in extra time.

Pau Cubarsi, 7: The Barcelona youngster has benefitted from Spain’s settled displays and has formed a superb partnership with Laporte. He was once again mostly untroubled throughout this game as La Roja didn’t face a single shot within 90 minutes. He did well to nip in and beat Fernandez in the challenge that led to the red card, and helped make a decisive late block to keep Spain ahead.

open image in gallery Pau Cubarsi was the man fouled for Enzo Fernandez’s red card ( Reuters )

Aymeric Laporte, 7: As with Cubarsi, he was almost entirely untroubled during his time on the pitch, as a consequence of both his own composure and skill as well as Spain’s near-flawless gameplan. Was forced to block off Messi late on at the expense of a yellow, but it was worth it, and he was later subbed in extra time. An impressive end to a near-flawless tournament for the Bilbao man.

Marc Cucurella, 7: Like his teammates, the full-back defended diligently when called upon, though he was rarely called upon. Instead, he was more impressive in possession, flashing an effort wide of the far post and constantly offering an outlet for his teammates, even in the final third.

Rodri, 8: The Spain midfielder may well be chasing another Ballon d’Or, and performances like this will certainly help his cause. He was at the centre of everything for much of the game, leading the Spain build-up, mopping up loose balls and breaking up rare Argentina attacks. This type of midfield performance is not as lauded as ones with goals or assists, but it’s so important to how this Spain team functions, and has led them to a second World Cup triumph.

open image in gallery Rodri produced another imperious showing as he helped Spain dominate Argentina ( Getty )

Dani Olmo, 6: The Barcelona man could have had an assist early on after a lovely lay-off to Yamal. He is to the Spain attack what Rodri is to the defence and the build-up, though today it didn’t click in the final third despite Spain’s dominance of the ball.

Fabian Ruiz, 6: Helped Spain dominate possession in the opening stages as they suffocated Argentina. Showed flashes of his ability during some slick passing moves, and is another who showed why he’s important to the Spain set-up, even if he was unable to directly affect the game before coming off.

Lamine Yamal, 6: Should probably have made it 1-0 with an early chance, though it was blocked well by Martinez. He provided a constant threat down the right but he was not his usual self, albeit he often found Argentina doubling up – or even tripling up – in defence. A quiet day for the 19-year-old, though he can afford a few of those in a team this talented.

open image in gallery Yamal found himself frustrated as the Argentina defence doubled up on him ( Getty )

Mikel Oyarzabal, 6: It wasn’t to be for the Real Sociedad man, who could not repeat his heroics from the Euro 2024 final. He was fairly anonymous throughout, with his only effort of note testing Martinez outside the box. Showed flashes of why he’s important to the team but was not able to get as involved in attacks as he’d have liked.

Alex Baena, 6: The Atletico Madrid man didn’t have a lot to do in terms of defensive duties, but he was largely ineffective in attack during his time on the pitch, though he did dovetail well with Cucurella down the left.

Subs

Ferran Torres, 8: The nature of Spain’s play arguably means that their designated ‘centre-forward’ is one of the least involved players at times, and so it proved as both Oyarzabal and Torres struggled to impose themselves in attack. However, the Barcelona man has proven adept at picking his moment at club level, and he did so again as he arrived in the box to fire in an accomplished finish for the winner.

open image in gallery Torres smashed in the opening goal in the 106th minute as Spain dominated a tired Argentina ( AP )

Pedri, 7: Pedri is another player who might have been surprised by the number of minutes he’s seen this summer, but he slotted in seamlessly after coming on and was brilliant throughout, hardly putting a foot wrong as Spain began to turn the screw. He may not benefit from the synergy between Rodri, Ruiz and Olmo at the moment, but the Barcelona youngster will lead this team for years to come.

Mikel Merino, 7: The Arsenal man has been Spain’s surprise package so far this tournament and he was unlucky to have a foul ruled against him in the build-up to the disallowed goal. Headed wide from a great Williams cross when he probably should have scored.

Nico Williams, 8: The winger changed Spain’s attack after coming on, with his skilful dribbling, pace and directness causing problems as soon as he entered the pitch. He was unlucky to have a goal ruled out, and equally unlucky to see a superb cross headed wide by Merino, though he eventually got his assist after great work at the back post in heading down the cross for Torres’ winner. While he has had to sit on the bench at times throughout this tournament, this was another memorable final performance for the world and European champion.

Martin Zubimendi, 6: Came on to replace Rodri, and as was the case with the Euro 2024 final, slotted seamlessly into midfield. Probably benefitted from Spain’s numerical advantage, but was solid enough.

Eric Garcia, 6: Came on to shore up the defence but had little to do as Argentina tired and Spain’s numerical advantage told.

Manager rating: Luis de la Fuente, 9: The flawless display from Spain was largely down to a manager who has proven himself as one of the best in the world in recent years. La Roja were imperious as they nullified all of Argentina’s threats in a dominant display, limiting Argentina to just two shots and none on target while providing plenty of attacking threat. His subs were inspired too, with two combining to score the goal that won them the World Cup.

open image in gallery Luis de la Fuente got all the big decisions right ( Reuters )

Argentina

Emi Martinez, 7: Eventually made a good stop from Yamal after Martinez’s deflection early on. Made a routine save from Torres’ close-range header before fumbling another long-range effort, but made a great save from a late Yamal free-kick. Made another good save from Williams early into extra time, a second in the lead-up to the disallowed goal, and could do little about the winner from Torres.

Gonzalo Montiel, 6: The defender was another who came into the side after a good cameo against England, but he had little to do early on up against an ineffective Alex Baena. Nevertheless, he was alert to make a clearance and stop Cucurella from having a free effort at goal in the second half just before he came off.

Cristian Romero, 6: The Tottenham man was not troubled too much in the first half despite Spain’s possession, and dovetailed well again with Martinez before the latter came off. He was subbed after the second hydration break, presumably due to injury of some sort, in a disappointing end to another tournament to remember. Can hold his head high alongside Martinez.

open image in gallery Both Romero and Martinez were forced off as Argentina were victim of a defensive injury crisis ( Reuters )

Lisandro Martinez, 6: A huge disappointment for the Manchester United defender, who was forced off inside the first half due to injury. He did make a solid contribution though, providing a decisive block early on to help Martinez stop a golden chance for Yamal. He was not troubled too much in the first half despite Spain’s possession, though was first to be booked after scything down Oyarzabal on the counter.

Nicolas Tagliafico, 5: Struggled up against Yamal early on, and somehow escaped a yellow card after bringing him down on the counter. Was helped out when they doubled up in defence, but offered little in attack and is another who will likely be retiring soon.

Nico Gonzalez, 5: His brief cameo against England was enough to earn the winger a starting berth but he was largely ineffective as Argentina toiled in the first half, before being replaced by Leandro Paredes at half-time.

Alexis Mac Allister, 6: The midfielder was probably lucky to escape an early yellow, and even more so after what looked like a fairly deliberate handball. However, he provided some badly needed composure in the first half, though he was also limited in what he could do in the face of Spain’s dominance.

Enzo Fernandez, 3: Having been the hero against England in an impressive outing, the Chelsea man was largely anonymous throughout the opening 90 minutes as himself and his midfield partners struggled to gain a foothold in the game. In the end it was a pathetic, petulant exit as dissent and a ridiculous foul saw him sent off in stoppage time, just as Argentina looked like they might be making their way into the game.

open image in gallery A rash challenge from Fernandez earned the Argentina midfielder a second yellow card in stoppage time ( Reuters )

Rodrigo De Paul, 5: Couldn’t impose himself on this game as he did in his cameo against England, and could do little to help his side as Spain dominated possession. Largely anonymous, but through no fault of his own.

Lionel Messi, 5: The 39-year-old was kept unusually quiet in the first half as his side were stifled, and it was more of the same in the second half as Spain began to turn the screw and nullify their opponents. In the end it was a step too far for the little genius, who couldn’t do it all on his own this time, and was limited by a near-perfect tactical display from La Roja.

Julian Alvarez, 5: Another who was unable to make any sort of impact during his time on the pitch. It was a notably muted performance, but he got little help from his midfield and even his attacking partners.

Subs

Nicolas Otamendi, 6: Cleared well from a slick Spain attack and overall performed well in extremely difficult circumstances, though was powerless to prevent the defeat in the end.

Leandro Paredes, 4: Came on at half-time and his first meaningful act was to get a yellow for a needless challenge and reaction. Struggled throughout, though perhaps through no fault of his own as Spain completely nullified their opponents. His time at this level is done, and he showed his frustration at the final whistle.

open image in gallery Paredes was involved in clashes after full-time ( Reuters )

Giuliano Simeone, 5: The winger was a victim of his side’s muted performance, though he offered little in attack or as an outlet, and lacked composure as he blasted over from near the penalty spot in extra-time stoppage time.

Facundo Medina, 5: Was up against it as he came on for Romero, and while he did well to hold firm for so long, he could do little about the goal.

Nahuel Molina, 4: Another who was up against it as Spain began to dominate but lost Williams as the Spain winger headed down for the opener.

Marcos Senesi, 5: Could do little as he was forced to defend wave after wave of Spain pressure.

Manager rating: Lionel Scaloni, 5: The Argentina boss has previously proven himself an astute manager but he was outclassed here by his Spanish counterpart. Part of that is down to his inferior squad options, but his changes made little difference and he was powerless to prevent his side delivering an abject performance.

News.title: Spain win World Cup in triumph of football over Argentine felony
News.content:
Spain should have won far more comfortably but the European champions lived up to the claim made by their coach Luis de la Fuente and proved they are the best team in the world – as they won this tournament for the second time and for the first since 2010 – having beaten the favourites France in the last four. They were worthy winners.

There is another European nation chasing that second star, the one beaten by Argentina in Atlanta last Wednesday.

If England ever want to win this again then here is the blueprint. From Spain. This is how the game should be played. Get the ball, keep the ball, love the ball, move the ball. Try to play. Be brave and stay brave. It is not complicated, but it requires a re-education.

Maybe one day English football will grow up and cherish ball-players of their own rather than Manchester City sign Rodri, who was magnificent here until he tired, or Arsenal Martín Zubimendi, who successfully replaced him.

Rodri was rightly named player of the tournament, in recognition of the football his nation played and the 30-year-old’s importance to that. He is their heartbeat and metronome. England do not just need to find a Rodri but cherish whoever that is.

News.title: Hamilton takes out Russell as Antonelli stretches lead with Belgian GP win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix from Spa-Francorchamps. The story of yesterday and in fact the weekend was of everyone trying to dislodge Kimi Antonelli from the top of the timesheets. Spoiler alert if you did not watch qualifying: they failed.

That is not to say the fight wasn’t a half-decent one. Max Verstappen and Red Bull were the closest challengers in the end, demonstrating an element of revival during a tricky season. Whether that will continue during the race is hard to know. Verstappen certainly thought he would have been further down the field without the tremendous tow he received from Isack Hadjar, his Red Bull team-mate, in the final sector.

Lando Norris also pushed Verstappen, though was almost half a second down on Antonelli’s time in the end. Unfortunately he will not be able to take advantage of a start from third place because he takes a 10-place grid penalty. George Russell, who has managed to reduce his Mercedes team-mate’s advantage to just 25 points in the past few rounds, was fourth and will start third. He did however, have a difficult session once again, finishing more than half a second off his team-mate.

He was at a loss to explain this. Well, he knows where he lost most of the time: on the straights. But he still does not understand exactly why it is happening. The good news for him is that third place is often the most optimal starting position at this track.

Will that be the case today? Let’s see...

News.title: Ryan Fox matches father Grant’s sporting folklore with Claret Jug
News.content:
It’s the final day of the Open Championship, golf’s oldest and most-prestigious major. The leaderboard offers up hope of a seesaw day where little-known-of golfers tussle it out with big names under the north-west English sun. All in all, it should be an exciting day.

But, as with the past two days, we head into the round with talk dominated by a certain Bryson DeChambeau. It’s as frustrating and annoying as it is, in these days dominated by social media/content etc etc, painfully predictable. So let’s get the DeChambeau news out the way. Having been fairly hit with a two-shot penalty for improving his lie on Friday, the YouTube content creator had a tantrum, threatened to withdraw, caused a delay in the release of third-round tee times, before turning up and shooting a one-under 69 to lie four behind the leader heading into today.

That’s not all, The Bryson DeChambeau Show carried on after yesterday’s round where James Corrigan takes up the script...

Bryson DeChambeau marched straight to the offices of the R&A after being heckled with a cry of “you’re a cheat” on Birkdale’s 18th green on Saturday. As the controversy over his two-shot penalty from Friday’s second round rumbled on, Telegraph Sport understands DeChambeau, who shot a third-round 69 to lie four shots off the lead of the Open, asked R&A chief executive Mark Darbon for his scorecard from Friday. It is against policy so his request was rejected. DeChambeau then went back to the recorder’s hut and asked if they had it. Again, the answer was in the negative. It is unclear why he wanted it, but a theory emerged that he wished to put it on his social media channels.

All in all it is pathetic posturing that you’d expect from a stroppy teenager. He’s only three off the lead and has the game to win at Royal Birkdale, he’d do well to forget the perceived slights (whatever they may be) and get on with trying to win the Claret Jug.

Oh, and to add another scene to the soap opera Rory McIlroy doubtless spoke for many inside and outside the rope when he called out DeChambeau saying: “Yeah, look, I won’t pretend to be up here and defend Bryson. I’m not particularly fond of him. I think a lot of it’s performative. I think a lot of it’s for attention. To hold the tournament hostage like that, and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn’t feel like it was a great look.”

So, I think it’s best we focus on the golf today and not the theatrics and sorry antics of the American.

Sam Burns, his playing partner yesterday, was brilliant as he backed up his 62 of Friday with a five-under 65. He leads by two on 10 under and is the man to beat. Lurking behind with intent are a host of big names and big hitters – Ryan Fox (eight under), Si Woo Kim (eight under), Lucas Herbert (six under), Ludvig Aberg (seven under) and the man himself YouTube’s very own DeChambeau (six under).

Also in with a hint of a hope is Tommy Fleetwood, the hometown boy in search of his first major, the Englishman will start the round on five under.

Stay here for all the action, where I hope all the talk during and after the day’s round is focused on the winner’s brilliance rather than the emotions of DeChambeau.

News.title: Records tumble at Lord’s as England win thriller against India
News.content:
When he fell, bowled trying to sweep Bethell, India were 260 for two, still a tough ask but not impossible, especially against an England side with plenty of demons. Kohli fired up in Rohit’s absence, hitting Will Jacks for two sixes and Bethell into the pavilion.

But the run-rate faltered as Curran whipped out his slower-ball bag of tricks. He had Ishan Kishan and Shreyas Iyer caught in the deep by sub Rehan Ahmed in the 44th over and Kohli in the next, slapping a catch to cover. The rest subsided, India short in the end at 360 for seven.

England’s ODI side have struggled for runs under Brendon McCullum and this was easily their best batting performance, not just for the collection of records but for the calm, controlled way they went about setting a huge total. The openers Duckett and Bethell gave them a 192-run cushion, Root was impregnable again and Buttler finished it off, proving what he can do when others give him a platform. India were without Jasprit Bumrah but that should not take the shine off England’s achievements.

This was the first Duckett-Bethell opening contribution and it was England’s highest for the first wicket since the last World Cup. Jason Roy and Jonny Bairstow were such an important part of the route to World Cup glory and they left a huge hole in the side. Duckett and Bethell are more touch players, capable of gear shifts rather than setting out at turbo pace like Roy and Bairstow. The fact they bat so often together in Test cricket, where Bethell appears at No 3, helps the level of understanding.

Duckett’s innings knocked Viv Richards’s 138 in the 1979 World Cup final off the top spot at Lord’s and continued the form he showed at the end of the New Zealand Test series when he scored his first Test hundred in nearly a year. He was out first ball in the second ODI in Cardiff but was never in any real bother at Lord’s as he compiled a fourth century in this format.

News.title: England win gives Borthwick breathing space after late try controversy
News.content:
And in doing so he may have just saved Borthwick’s job.

The Rugby Football Union, following its review into England’s Six Nations campaign that yielded just one victory, had publicly offered its backing to its head coach through to the World Cup. But in reality, there are no guarantees. It needed evidence of England’s progress.

Two wins from three rounds of the Nations Championship is likely to convince RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney to back his man. But Borthwick will know that nothing can be taken for granted.

Four years ago, Eddie Jones, facing similar scrutiny from his employers, looked to have salvaged his job by winning the last two matches in a three-Test summer tour of Australia. But it did still not save him from the sack the following November.

Still. There was enough character and attacking prowess to convince the RFU that, despite the flaws in this display, the team are on the right track again.

It was still far from an 80-minute performance, but this was England’s first away victory in a year, in a hostile environment and after all the challenges, both physical and mental, the players have faced in travelling to three continents over three weeks – clocking up more than 25,000 miles – at the end of a long season.

England wobbled alarmingly earlier in the second half but remarkably found the resilience to drag themselves back into the game just as it looked like it was slipping from their grasp. That is clear evidence of players playing for their coach and each other.

Discipline, however, remains a major problem for Borthwick’s England. They had been cruising to what would looked to have been a statement victory at half-time following tries by Tommy Freeman and two by Ben Earl, in what had been their finest half of rugby this year.

And yet, once again indiscipline undermined their efforts. Remarkably, they were shown four yellow cards – Jack van Poortvliet, Alex Coles, Pollock (to more booing) and Emmanuel Iyogun – in the second half to take their total to 14 in their last 10 Tests, and at one stage were down to 12 men but, significantly, this time it did not prove fatal.

News.title: Tuchel learns lesson as England clinch third place in 10-goal thriller
News.content:
Neither England nor France wanted to be playing this game in Miami, but they can have no complaints about the nature of their semi-final defeats.

Tournament favourites France were comprehensively outplayed by Spain, with their feted front four of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Bradley Barcola and Michael Olise all turning in below-par performances.

England’s defeat by Argentina was perhaps not as much of a surprise, but the nature of Thomas Tuchel’s team’s second-half collapse was just as alarming as France’s no-show.

England’s manager was fiercely criticised for replacing Anthony Gordon with Ezri Konsa and switching to a back five in the 72nd minute, but Tuchel has since defended his decisions.

“If you are asking if I regret my decisions, if this is the question, then I say no. I don’t regret my ‌decisions because I ‌felt that we became ⁠too passive,” said Tuchel.

“I took several decisions, trusting my instinct, my intuition, my experience, trusting my competitiveness, and I took the decision in order to help the team and get the result.

“I would regret if I didn’t help. I would regret ⁠if we didn’t react, but I have no regrets over the decision itself.”

Quite how strong Didier Deschamps and Tuchel decide to go with their teams is anyone’s guess. There has been some suggestion that Mbappe will start to give him the chance to beat Lionel Messi to the Golden Boot.

Some of England’s regular starters, such as Declan Rice, look physically spent, so there could be some rotation, and even a chance for players such as Kobbie Mainoo who has not played a minute of football at the tournament.

The third/fourth-place play-off has been rebranded as the “Bronze Final” for this tournament, and Tuchel was keen to point out that finishing third would be England’s best World Cup result since 1966. They lost this fixture against Belgium in 2018, but the way that game has been widely forgotten speaks volumes.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Scotland fight back to claim victory against Fiji in Nations Championship
News.content:
A barrelling Schoeman finished an initial break by match captain Stafford McDowall, then Dobie burrowed over beside the posts in the 61st minute to put Scotland in front for the first time in 40 minutes.

Scotland glossed up the scoreline with two more tries in the last six minutes by Cummings and Dobie again to send home a crowd of 55,000 happy.

“I thought our bench did really well,” Townsend told the BBC. “Something I’ve learned over the last 12 months, the bench can help you change momentum. The players can come up with solutions themselves but the bench can give you energy and solutions but also bravery. We’re a team that will back our decisions and that put real pressure on Fiji.

“I felt [Fiji] picked their strongest side today and it took a lot of work for us to break them down but also it took a really good defensive performance,” Townsend added. “Fiji didn’t really break us that often [and] in that final quarter the guys were outstanding. We’ll take a few positives from that.”

Fiji had never beaten Scotland at Murrayfield but would have sensed the chance of making history by half-time. The Fijians were tough and clinical in a huge turnaround from last weekend when they were humiliated by England 73-8 in Liverpool.

Sports.title: World Cup final LIVE: Lionel Messi in tears as Spain crowned champions vs Argentina
Sports.content:
Spain have been crowned the champions of the world two years after securing the European crown having dominated Argentina in the final in New Jersey, with Ferran Torres' goal enough

Spain have won the World Cup with a slender victory against Argentina in New Jersey.

Ferran Torres gave the European champions the lead just minutes into the second period of extra time. His goal came after nearly two hours of goalless football at MetLife Stadium. Argentina were reduced to ten men before the extra 30 minutes, with Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez sent off for two bookable offence.

There was also some drama before the game. Spain's pre-match training session was forced to be cancelled due to storms, while fans and members of the media have stumbled into serious issues getting into the stadium. Meanwhile, the pre-match closing ceremonies have ran over, with delays impacting the game itself.

Sports.title: Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni breaks down in tears during quit hint after World Cup final
Sports.content:
Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni breaks down in tears during quit hint after World Cup final

Lionel Scaloni's Argentina contract expires in December and he's indicated he could yet depart his role after failing to guide his team a second consecutive World Cup

View 2 Images Lionel Scaloni was deeply emotional after Argentina's World Cup final defeat to Spain

Lionel Scaloni has hinted he could quit his role as Argentina head coach upon the expiry of his contract later this year.

‌



The 48-year-old, who has guided La Albiceleste to two Copa Americas, one World Cup and La Finalissima since taking up the role in 2018, has a deal which runs until December.

‌



While Scaloni will speak to the Argentinian Football Association regarding fresh terms, he insists there is a chance he could call time on his illustrious spell at the helm.

‌



He said during an emotional post-match press conference: "I haven't spoken with Leo [Messi]. As for me, I'm going to talk to the president. I have an idea of what I want to do.

What Argentina star said to Rodri in furious on-pitch exchange after World Cup final whistle READ MORE :

Donald Trump crashes Spain's World Cup trophy moment and humiliates FIFA boss READ MORE :

"I'll fulfil the contract and then we'll see. The truth is, I feel the need to think, because I don't know if I'll be able to do something as big as this.

"Maybe we'll have to talk. I'm grateful to the president for giving me an opportunity like this, for being in this position," before he broke down in tears.

‌



He then continued: "Being in the place I am, a dream come true for everyone. We tried until the very last moment to give our all as a coaching staff and as players. It's only right that I can take this time to think about it. This place is wonderful, a dream come true that I never imagined in my life."

View 2 Images Lionel Scaloni's Argentina contract runs until December

Scaloni then added before abruptly leaving the press conference room: "In my life I never thought, we all thought on the coaching staff, that we'd be in this position.

‌



"So, to continue, a lot of things are needed, especially to reset, to rebuild a group like this, which is unlikely to be formed again, and it pains me deeply."

Argentina were totally outplayed in the World Cup final and had just two shots to Spain's 20.

La Roja had to be patient to eventually break down the door, however, much to the brilliance and resilience of Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez.

Article continues below

Ferran Torres eventually struck the winner after coming off the bench, inflicting the killer blow in the 106th minute after Enzo Fernandez was sent off following two yellow cards.

Sports.title: BBC and ITV pundits unite after spotting 'disgusting' Argentina World Cup move
Sports.content:
BBC and ITV pundits unite after spotting 'disgusting' Argentina World Cup move

Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in New Jersey, but celebrations were marred when two Argentinian defenders clashed with Spanish stars, prompting an outcry from pundits on the BBC and ITV

View 3 Images Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes was sent off for kicking and punching Spanish stars. (Image: (Photo by CHARLY TRIBALLEAU / AFP via Getty Images))

BBC pundits have slammed Argentina’s behaviour as “disgusting” following their World Cup final defeat to Spain.

‌



The defending champions, led by Lionel Messi, suffered a 1-0 extra-time loss in New Jersey after Ferran Torres struck in the 106th minute. Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez was sent off just before the additional period for a second yellow card in a game dominated by 'spoiling tactics'.

‌



There were more unsavoury scenes at full-time involving Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina. Argentina defender Molina struck Spain midfielder Rodri as he ran on to the pitch to celebrate his side’s success.

‌



Paredes also appeared to grab Eric Garcia by the throat and then threw Gavi to the ground. After the match, BBC pundits digested the ugly events.

Ex-England goalkeeper Joe Hart said: “There was one man on the pitch who did have class and that was Lionel Messi, who shook hands with every one of those Spanish players.

“The game’s done. They could have absolutely no complaints about what happened today. Disgusting behaviour.”

‌



Hart added: “Spain fully deserve it. They have been absolutely superb all tournament.

“They have dominated all game against a rigid, rugged Argentina. The best team has won this World Cup.”

Argentina were previously criticised for their aggressive behaviour during their 2-1 semi-final win over England, after which players unveiled a banner claiming sovereignty of the Falklands Islands. FIFA investigated the banner later.

‌



Fellow pundit and former England star Wayne Rooney said of Argentina’s behaviour: “Does it surprise you? It doesn’t surprise me.

“We’ve seen this with Argentina before. It’s just not the reaction you want. We’ve seen some of the reaction after knocking England out in the last round.

“That’s just sad. If you lose a game of football, be graceful and get out of there. It’s really poor from them.”

‌



View 3 Images Leandro Paredes and Eric Garcia have words after the FIFA World Cup 2026 Final match (Image: Al Bello/Getty Images)

“That’s a reaction to them being outplayed, out-fought, out-thought on the football pitch, and then they resort to that at the end,” continued Rooney.

‌



“It’s poor from those two players.”

Micah Richards added: “It’s quite embarrassing really. In the game, they were just on the cusp every single time.

“Paredes doesn’t need to do that, he’s better than that, and it doesn’t stop there – it keeps going and going and going.

‌



“We all know what it’s like to lose a game, we can be very frustrated, but this is not good enough – it’s not a good look at all.”

ITV's pundits and commentators shared a similar view. Gary Neville, speaking on ITV, singled out Paredes’ behaviour for criticism.

The former England full-back said: “They’re very competitive and I love that element of them, but (Paredes) has just been a disgrace for the last couple of games, and why the referees have allowed him to continue doing what he is doing…”

‌



View 3 Images Players had to be seperated at full-time (Image: Michael Zemanek/Shutterstock)

ITV’s co-commentators were in agreement that Spain were deserved winners, with Lee Dixon accusing Argentina of “anti-football” and questioning how Paredes had remained on the pitch, while Ally McCoist said Spain were “the only team trying to win this game”.

Dixon said: “You have to say, especially after those scenes just then, well done Spain. Football has been the winner, there’s no doubt about that. They’re a deserved team to win it on the day.

Article continues below

“Throughout the tournament they’ve gotten better and better, conceding one goal in a World Cup tournament just says everything you need to know about how organised and creative they are.

“They’ve got pace down the wings and they’re good to watch. On the other hand, today, Argentina were just anti-football, and the scenes at the end, how Paredes is still on the pitch, I’ll never know. I made out six or seven times he should have been sent off.

“(Messi’s) legacy coming to an end. Wasn’t as his best today, wasn’t allowed to be.”

Sports.title: Donald Trump brutally booed before hijacking trophy presentation at World Cup final
Sports.content:
Donald Trump brutally booed before hijacking trophy presentation at World Cup final

Donald Trump brutally booed before hijacking trophy presentation at World Cup final

View Image US President Donald Trump stands by the FIFA World Cup Trophy before the game (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

US President Donald Trump walked out to a stadium full of boos and jeers following the last whistle of the 2026 World Cup.

Footage shared on social media showed crowds heckling the 47th President of the United States as he walked across the grass to the centre of the pitch in order to present Spain with the World Cup trophy.

Seemingly unbothered by the hissing crowd, Trump then refused to leave the podium after presenting Spain with the World Cup trophy, making his presence at the World Cup even more awkward.

Spain claimed the title after beating the defending champions in extra time, with Ferran Torres scoring the decisive goal after Argentina were reduced to 10 men when Enzo Fernandez was sent off in the 93rd minute.

After the final whistle, the Spanish players walked onto the podium individually to collect their medals before US President Trump and Gianni Infantino presented them with the World Cup trophy.

Article continues below

But instead of stepping aside once the presentation was over, Trump stayed on stage, shaking hands with players and raising his fists in the air as the celebrations got underway.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Infantino appeared to try to usher a seemingly uncertain Trump away from the team, but the US President remained standing to the right of the squad as they celebrated, overshadowing what was meant to be Spain's trophy-lift moment.

Sports.title: Second Argentina player sent off as Leandro Paredes brawls with Garcia and Gavi
Sports.content:
Second Argentina player sent off as Leandro Paredes brawls with Garcia and Gavi

Spain's World Cup final win over Argentina was marred by violence after the final whistle

View 3 Images Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes was sent off for kicking and punching Spanish stars after the World Cup final (Image: (Photo by CHARLY TRIBALLEAU / AFP via Getty Images))

There were ugly scenes after the final whistle in the World Cup final, with Leandro Paredes shown a red card for throwing punches at Spanish stars Eric Garcia and Gavi. It was the second red card for Argentina as Spain ran out 1-0 winners in a one-sided affair, with Ferran Torres scoring the winner in the second half of extra time.

‌



Argentina had to play the additional phase of the game with ten men after Enzo Fernandez was shown a red card for two yellow card offences just before the final whistle in normal time. The Chelsea midfielder had been booked for dissent before a rash challenge on the halfway line on Pau Cubarsi, with referee Slavko Vincic giving the 25-year-old his marching orders.

‌



Argentina tried to hang on to take the game to penalties, but Torres' winner meant Spain would claim their second World Cup title, sparking wild scenes at full-time. Spanish players raced onto the pitch to celebrate when Argentinian defender Nahuel Molina appeared to punch Rodri in the stomach.

‌



BREAKING: Lionel Messi bursts into tears after Argentina lose World Cup final to Spain READ MORE :

World Cup final ends in chaos as Argentina star throws punches after Spain win READ MORE :

The Man City star reacted and turned to confront the Argentinian, while Spain defender Eric Garcia rushed to intervene and separate the two players. Argentinian midfielder joins in the fracas, kicking and grabbing Garcia by the throat as Lionel Scaloni tries to diffuse the melee.

Unused Spain substitute Gavi tried to intervene and push Paredes, with the 32-year-old retaliating, throwing punches and pushing the 21-year-old to the floor before players from both teams steam in to separate proceedings.

View 3 Images Leandro Paredes got involved in an ugly clash with Gavi after the World Cup final (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"Does is surprise you?" Rooney asked his BBC pundits at full-time. "It doesn't surprise me, I think we've seen this with Argentina before and it's just not the reaction you want.

"We've seen some of the reaction after knocking England out in the last round as well. I think Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves as well, so it's disappointing.

"But that's just sad. If you lose a game of football, be graceful and get out of there. It's very poor from them."

‌



Fellow pundit Joe Hart said: "Disgusting. There was one man on the pitch who did have class, and that was Lionel Mess - shook hands of every one of those Spanish players.

"The game's done, they can have absolutely no complaints about what happened today. Disgusting behaviour.

"Rodri, I don't think, needed to get in their faces, but when you've been wound up for 120 minutes, and you felt you've been wronged, and you've felt the referee's on your back, and you've got that win, referee's blown his whistle, leave it.

‌



"And I think Argentina...are you surprised they've gone over the line again?"

View 3 Images Leandro Paredes was sent off for his part in the brawl (Image: Getty Images)

"It's quite embarrassing really, because for all I give Argentina that praise in terms of how they approach the game," Michah Richards added. "Yes, they know Spain are a batter team on the ball, but what can they do to destruct them off the ball? And in the game, they were just on the cusp every single time.

‌



"The first yellow card wasn't until 40 odd minutes in the first-half, but seeing that sort of stuff after the game's been played and someone's just been crowned World Cup champions, it's not good enough. It's quite embarrassing to be honest.

"Paraedes there, he doesn't need to do that, he's better than that. And it doesn't stop there, it keeps going, and going, and going.

"And we all know what it's like to lose a game, we can be very frustrated, we understand that. But this is not good enough, it's not a good look at all."

Article continues below

Sports.title: Donald Trump causes scene at World Cup final by photobombing trophy lift
Sports.content:
Donald Trump causes scene at World Cup final by photobombing trophy lift

Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in a fairly forgettable World Cup final after extra-time and were handed the coveted trophy by the President of the United States Donald Trump

View 2 Images Rodri lifts the World Cup with Donald Trump still on the platform (Image: Getty Images)

Donald Trump gatecrashed another trophy presentation as the United States President decided to hang around for the start of the celebrations after Spain beat Argentina in the World Cup final.

‌



The 80-year-old caused a stir last summer when Chelsea won the Fifa Club World Cup, which was held across the United States, by staying put after handing the gold over and was even seen bobbing along while Chelsea's players celebrated their achievement.

‌



Trump repeated the trick in New Jersey after handing Spain's captain, Rodri, the coveted Jules Rimet trophy, albeit he didn't stick around for quite as long this time around. He lingered on the edge of the platform for a few moments as Spain celebrated before being ushered along gently by a laughing Gianni Infantino.

‌



It was confirmed last month that Trump would once again present the trophy to the winners of the tournament.

World Cup final LIVE: Lionel Messi in tears as Spain crowned champions vs Argentina READ MORE :

Infantino, Fifa's president, was the one who confirmed Trump would do the honours for Sunday's final. “That’s always been the plan,” he said.

“That’s how it’s always been done in the past – the president of the country where the final is held presents the trophy together with the FIFA president.”

‌



Trump, who was booed by fans when shown on the big screen at MetLife Stadium, was in attendance for the World Cup final alongside Infantino.

View 2 Images Spain beat Argentina in extra-time to win the World Cup (Image: Alex Pantling/FIFA)

Unfortunately, he and the tens of thousands of others in attendance were treated to a fairly drab final, which was mercifully ended in extra-time by Spain's Ferran Torres.

Article continues below

The Barcelona struck in the 106th minute to give Spain a deserved breakthrough against the 10 men of Argentina, who saw Enzo Fernandez dismissed for a second yellow card in the final moments of regulation time.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi bursts into tears after Argentina lose World Cup final to Spain
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi bursts into tears after Argentina lose World Cup final to Spain

Spain defeated Argentina in the World Cup final, with Lionel Messi unable to lead his team to a successful title defence after Ferran Torres' goal at MetLife Stadium

View 2 Images Lionel Messi couldn't hold back his tears after Argentina lost to Spain (Image: BBC)

Argentina icon Lionel Messi burst into tears following his side's World Cup final defeat to Spain. The Inter Miami star managed to keep a stiff upper lip during the immediate aftermath but was unable to hold in his cry in the period after receiving his runners-up medal.

‌



Messi, 39, may have already played his final World Cup match, though he proved throughout the tournament that he was still able to contribute at the highest level. The attacker was kept out of the game against Spain for most of the match, though he provided some threatening moments as the South American side scrambled for an equaliser following Ferran Torres' extra-time strike.

‌



The former Barcelona star scored eight goals during the tournament, falling two short of Kylian Mbappe's golden boot-winning tally.

‌



While some of his team-mates threw punches, at the full-time whistle, Messi sat on the pitch and could only stare at the scenes around him in New Jersey. Messi rose from his feet to greet Spanish teenager Lamine Yamal who offered some comfort, rubbing the Argentina captain's back while in an embrace.

World Cup final ends in chaos as Argentina star throws punches after Spain win READ MORE :

World Cup fans issue the same complaint about half-time show as Spain vs Argentina delayed READ MORE :

Joe Hart highlighted Messi's composure at the end of the game, in contrast to the violent scenes involving Leandro Paredes. The former goalkeeper said: "Disgusting.

"There was one man on the pitch who did have class, and that was Lionel Messi - shook hands of every one of those Spanish players.

‌



"The game's done, they can have absolutely no complaints about what happened today. Disgusting behaviour."

View 2 Images Lionel Messi looks at his second place medal after losing to Spain in the World Cup final (Image: PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA / AFP via Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Matchwinner Torres highlighted Messi as a massive opponent to overcome on the biggest stage. He said: "I think in the end the goal came from 47 million people, not just those of us that are here.

"Today destiny was written, it was made for us to win. We're far from our people today but we tried to be as close as possible to them.

"Finals are hard. When you have Messi on the opposing team you do get worried but we always backed ourselves and tried to show our football and I think we managed to do it once again."

Article continues below

In addition to a runners-up medal for his part in Argentina's run to the final, Messi also received the runners up spot for the Golden Ball, the award for the competition's best player. Spain star Rodri claimed that one.

Sports.title: Spain beat Argentina to win World Cup
Sports.content:
Spain won their second World Cup title after Ferran Torres' 106th-minute smashed finish earned a 1-0 win against defending champions Argentina in the 2026 final.

Spain were deserved winners. Torres scored with Spain's 20th shot while the game ended without Argentina registering a single shot on target.

Lionel Messi touched the ball just 54 times in a match that took three hours to complete and featured a 27-minute half-time break.

Spain's win had shades of their maiden victory in 2010 too, scoring in the second period of extra time after a goalless 90 minutes. Then, it was Andres Iniesta against the Netherlands - now another Barcelona player, Torres, adds his name to the history books.

Image: Spain's Rodri lifts the World Cup

A nod back from fellow substitute Nico Williams saw the former Manchester City forward storm on to the ball and fire past Aston Villa goalkeeper Emi Martinez. It came minutes after Williams had an initial strike ruled out for an alleged Mikel Merino foul on Nicolas Otamendi.

Argentina did keep their shape well as Spain applied consistent pressure - especially after Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez was sent off for a reckless second yellow at the end of normal time - and relied on Martinez to make a string of saves.

Image: Enzo Fernandez fouls Pau Cubarsi resulting in a red card for the Argentina midfielder

Image: Enzo Fernandez was sent off late in the second half as Argentina finished the game with ten players

Their only threat emerged in added-on time at the end of extra time, with Giuliano Simeone blazing over a shot that could have sent the game to penalties.

But there was no fairytale end to Messi's expected final World Cup appearance, with the Argentina skipper anonymous for much of the game. He was also beaten to his first World Cup Golden Boot by France's Kylian Mbappe, who won it by two goals.

Image: A tearful Lionel Messi reacts to Argentina's defeat in the World Cup final (AP Photo/Pamela Smith)

Spain remain undefeated under manager Luis de la Fuente in tournament matches and add a World Cup win to their Euros title from 2024. It has been quite the tournament from an opening draw to Cape Verde to making France and Argentina look like average teams and lifting the World Cup.

Paredes and Molina involved in angry scenes after full-time

Image: Leandro Parades was sent off after the game after starting a brawl with some of Spain's players

There were unsavoury scenes at full-time as Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina looked to strike out at the celebrating Spain players after Argentina's defeat.

Molina threw out an elbow and caught Rodri, while Paredes appeared to kick Eric Garcia to the floor and pushed him back with a strong hand around his neck when the Spaniard got back to his feet to confront him.

A Spain substitute was then held back by another Argentina player before Paredes came in, ripped his bib and swung for him twice, catching him in the face.

Paredes, who came on at half-time, was booked within minutes of coming on and escaped a number of other yellow card offenses. He was eventually sent off in the aftermath of the post-match hostilities.

Image: Spain's Ferran Torres celebrates scoring their winner (AP Photo/Julio Cortez)

5: SHOT! Lamine Yamal has the first shot on target.

39: SHOT! Oyarzabal strikes - but it goes straight at Emi Martinez.

77: CHANCE! Pedro and Pau Cubarsi draw saves from the Argentina goalkeeper as Spain keep pushing for a goal.

90+3: RED CARD! Fernandez sent off for second yellow card after reckless challenge on Cubarsi.

90+9: SAVE! Lamine Yamal forces a great save from Emi Martinez after a whipped effort.

96: NO GOAL! Williams has the ball in the net, but it is ruled out as Merino inadvertently catches Otamendi on the foot in the build-up.

106: GOAL! Torres fires home from Williams' cushioned effort.

114: OFFSIDE! Torres has the ball in the net again, but he is flagged offside.

120+2: OVER! Simeone has the chance to equalise, but sends an effort over the face of goal as Spain win the World Cup.

Image: Spain's Nico Williams reacts after seeing his strike on goal ruled out by VAR

Analysis: Spain worthy World Cup winners

Sky Sports' Adam Bate: "Spain began this World Cup with a goalless draw against Cape Verde but they end it as worthy winners. They beat the favourites in the semi-final and the reigning champions tonight.

"One goal conceded in eight games, never behind in the tournament, they played all the football here. Passed Argentina off the park. The European champions are World Cup winners too. Thoroughly deserved."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferran Torres scores a crucial goal in added time for Spain to make it 1-0 in the World Cup final game against Argentina.

Sky Sports' Gary Neville speaking on ITV: "Spain are not the best individual players, what they are is the best team, the best collective. And also the best system of play.

"I spent a very short time in Spain and what I found was that they were a different technical and tactical level to Premier League teams, their understanding of the game.

"That comes out most in international football when you are playing every four days in 35-degree heat. Technically and tactically, they are outstanding."

Three Spain players win World Cup awards Player of the tournament: Rodri

Golden Glove: Unai Simon

Young player: Pau Cubarsi

Image: Spain's Rodri poses with the award for the tournament's best player (AP Photo/Ashley Landis)

Image: Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon poses with the Golden Glove award (AP Photo/Ashley Landis)

Torres: Destiny was written for us to win

Spain forward Ferran Torres to FIFA: "I think in the end the goal came from 47 million people (approximately the population of Spain), not just those of us that are here.

"Today destiny was written, it was made for us to win. We're far from our people today, but we tried to be as close as possible to them.

Image: Ferran Torres celebrates his goal in extra time to win the World Cup for Spain

"Finals are hard. When you have [Lionel] Messi on the opposing team, you do get worried, but we always backed ourselves and tried to show our football and I think we managed to do it once again.

"[It was] a huge relief [to score]. I've been criticised throughout the whole tournament but, as I said before, destiny was written.

"Thanks to God, he always gives me the strength to continue and in the end he grants things to those that most deserve them."

Merino: We knew we were a better footballing side than Argentina

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Spanish fans go wild as they claim their second World Cup trophy over Argentina.

Spain's Mikel Merino speaking to ITV: "Unbelievable. It's the perfect moment for us.

"We are such a golden generation with these young players that give everything they have for this country, for these fans. Luckily, we got the trophy today.

"It was a game about concentration. We knew we were a better team in terms of football.

"The pitch was dry, it was a difficult game because they are a very, very competitive side and they know how to make the game difficult for you. I think the team was outstanding today and we deserve it.

"When you are facing a low block and you have a team that is defending in your own box, you have to attack the box with bodies on the line and then control the transitions.

"We have very good players that can cross the ball, big threats in the box and the old-school way of scoring goals and we did it."

Analysis: Messi conspicuous by his absence

Image: Argentina's Lionel Messi missed out on winning his first World Cup Golden Boot

Sky Sports' Charlotte Marsh: "The World Cup game perhaps epitomises the importance of Messi to Argentina in his anonymity.

"They have relied on the 39-year-old time and again in this tournament, and much like a few of his contemporaries, he did go missing in one of the biggest moments.

"However, that wasn't entirely his fault. Argentina had 34.9 per cent possession and were not able to work anything for their star man to use.

"In the final five minutes, Messi had a few glimpses but this time, he and Argentina ran out of time, with no shots registered on target.

"But by his absence and his team unable to provide for him, it shows even more just how much they rely on him for their goals."

Sports.title: 'My hands were all over the place!' - Fox savours dramatic Open win
Sports.content:
Ryan Fox admitted it was a "dream come true" as he defied the nerves to clinch a dramatic victory in The Open at Royal Birkdale.

The 39-year-old New Zealander produced a superb finish to the final round to overtake clubhouse leader Cameron Young and snatch a one-shot win.

Fox, who had carded a 62 on Saturday to put himself in contention to claim a maiden major success, looked to be slipping out of it after making his second bogey of the day at the 11th.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the final round of the 154th Open as Fox claimed the victory

Back-to-back birdies at the 13th and 14th put him back in the hunt and he then did well to escape with only a bogey at the 15th after a nightmare lie in a greenside bunker.

He hit back by birdieing the 16th following a brilliant approach and then, after missing a chance at the 17th, nailed two superb shots down the 18th before boldly draining a 12-foot putt to claim the Claret Jug.

"To play that last hole how I did, I stood on the tee and said to my caddie Dean (Smith), we're going to try to win this," said Fox.

"I hit two perfect shots. I'm not sure how I hit the putt. My hands were all over the place. I was just trying to get it towards the hole somewhere. It's surreal that it went in.

"My focus with the putter all day was just take a really deep breath before I hit it and just try to hit a line, and I did that.

Image: Fox celebrates after holing the winning putt

"I don't know how I managed to keep the putter face square enough for that to go on line, but I'll take it.

"Champion Golfer of the Year has got a pretty good ring to it. It is a dream come true.

"You do dream of this moment. I don't know whether I ever thought it was going to become a reality. Now it is, and to have my name etched in the history of the game is pretty awesome. I think it's pretty awesome for New Zealand as well. It's going to be big down there."

Fox is the son of former All Blacks fly-half Grant Fox and the grandson of former New Zealand Test captain Merv Wallace.

"We've got a great history in our family," he said. "I was lucky enough to carve my own path there. I don't know if this tops their achievements, but it's certainly right up there.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fox equalled the lowest round in Open history with a third-round 62 at Royal Birkdale

"I spoke to my kids last night, and they said bring back a trophy. I think this is a pretty cool one to bring back for them.

"I don't know if my dad would be able to contain himself when I was coming down the stretch. He's never been one who has been very good if he doesn't have control over things.

"I think when he was playing and in control of the output, under pressure he was fine. But when he doesn't have control, I think he's a nervous wreck. I'm sure he was."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player How Fox clinched victory in The Open at Royal Birkdale

'He stayed aggressive'

Sky Sports Golf duo Dame Laura Davies and Andrew Coltart were both full of praise for Fox and the aggressive approach he adopted on the back nine.

Davies said: "He was the most impressive player all day. He stayed aggressive; I don't think he was scared of losing it. If he lost it because he hit a shot that just didn't work out he was prepared to stay aggressive and I firmly believe that's why he did it.

"He hit irons when he had to, but when there was a chance, a sniff of a birdie, the driver was out, full commitment.

"And the way he played 18 I don't think you could have drawn that up any better. Two of the best shots he will ever hit in his life just to hit that green to give himself a chance."

Image: Fox proudly holds the Claret Jug

Coltart added: "I've never seen somebody push through the tape as hard as that right at the end of the tournament to win a major championship.

"At a place like this, too. It was just superb. The 62 on Saturday I think, helped cement his belief in his ability out there.

"While they all struggled with the pressure, he stood tall."

What's next?

The next PGA Tour event is the 3M Open at TPC Twin Cities in Minnesota, beginning Thursday, with early coverage on Sky Sports+ before switching to Sky Sports Golf at 7pm.

The 3M Open is part of a triple-header of live golf on Sky Sports, with the ISPS Handa Senior Open and ISPS Handa Women's Scottish Open also live. Sports.title: 'My heart really sank' - Hamilton relieved mechanic unhurt after hit
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says his "heart really sank" when his Ferrari hit a mechanic in a pit-stop incident that led to the team being fined heavily by Belgian Grand Prix stewards.

Hamilton's right-front tyre struck the mechanic - who was unhurt - after the driver was given the green signal to leave the team's pit box, briefly knocking the crew member, who was in front of the wheel in an attempt to make a front-wing adjustment, to his knees.

Hamilton promptly stopped his car as the mechanic was helped to his feet, before leaving the pit box.

The incident was placed under a post-race stewards' investigation with Ferrari later handed a €30,000 fine, €10,000 of which is suspended for a year.

Ferrari admitted to an "inappropriately late instruction for the wing adjustment, a lack of clear communication and the mechanic's failure to notice the green light" amid a "complex and unusual combination of circumstances" at a stop which Hamilton had first served a five-second penalty before work on the car commenced.

With no fault attributed to the driver, who stewards said had also suffered a "sporting disadvantage" anyway due to the fact he was delayed in leaving the pit stop, Hamilton retained his fourth-place finish in the race.

The result moved Hamilton back into second place ahead of George Russell in the Drivers' Championship with a deficit of 45 points to Kimi Antonelli, the race winner at Spa-Francorchamps.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix

Speaking about the pit stop confusion after the race, Hamilton said his mind had immediately flashed back to an incident at the 2018 Bahrain Grand Prix when a botched Ferrari stop for Kimi Raikkonen caused a mechanic, Francesco Cigarini, to suffer a double leg fracture.

Hamilton was therefore relieved to be told that the mechanic involved on Sunday was not injured, when he enquired about him over team radio.

"The green light went and so I went," said Hamilton to Sky Sports F1.

"You're looking over here [to the left at the lights] you're not looking over there so that's more probably on the team, ultimately.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Despite being given a five-second penalty for an opening lap collision with George Russell, Lewis Hamilton was left more frustrated with his performance over the weekend as he finished fourth in Belgium

"But when it happened, then I noticed him and I stopped and it just went through my mind in that moment was back when Kimi hit and [a mechanic] broke a leg and my heart really sank for a second.

"I'm really grateful he's OK."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton crashes at Turn 13 during the final practice session at the Belgian GP

'We could have been challenging for the win' - Hamilton rues consequence of his Saturday crash

Hamilton's stop had already been elongated by the fact that Ferrari's crew had first had to wait five seconds before starting the car's tyre change owing to the serving of a time penalty for causing a collision with Russell at Les Combes on the opening lap.

The clash spun Russell out of the race, although the Mercedes driver later blamed his own car's straight-line speed issues, rather than former team-mate Hamilton, for the incident at the end of the long Kemmel Straight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch from onboard with George Russell as he crashes out of the Belgian GP after contact with Lewis Hamilton

Hamilton also preferred not to focus on the specifics of the collision in his post-race interview, instead taking the blame for not qualifying higher than sixth, which became fifth on the grid due to Lando Norris' engine penalty, after crashing in Saturday's final practice session.

"I don't count on myself [being] unlucky, I think about my mistake that I made yesterday, so I take full responsibility really for the fourth place that I ended up getting," he said.

"I damaged the car then when they rebuilt the car they missed something on the suspension so the balance was completely different so it meant I was probably a good couple of tenths - maybe three tenths - slower than I should have been in qualifying.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Drama at the start of the Belgium GP as George Russell's title hopes take a huge blow

"Then I ended up further back, got in the incident. Five second penalty, so like a domino effect from a mistake from myself.

"But the team have been doing a great job with strategy, pit stops. We are continuing to improve the car. I think our pace today, without the damage, we could have been challenging for the win."
