Sports.title: Spain 1-0 Argentina PLAYER RATINGS: Which two stars received 3/10 after dreadful displays? Who was 'imperious' but faded? And which Premier League stalwart delivered a 'shocking' first-half?
Sports.content:
Ferran Torres wrote his name into Spanish football history after scoring in the 106th minute of the World Cup final to break the hearts of Argentina and Lionel Messi.

The substitute, who smashed his finish into the roof of the net, reclaimed deserved glory for La Roja for the first time since 2010 after their opponents managed just two shots across the entirety of the match.

Spain's elegance and discipline was contrasted with the brutish skulduggery of Argentina, who saw Enzo Fernandez sent off in the 93rd minute. His midfield counterpart, Leandro Paredes, was also shown his marching orders after a violent clash after full-time.

Daily Mail Sport's CRAIG HOPE was at the MetLife Stadium to bring you our player ratings.

Spain have won the World Cup after a deserved 1-0 victory over Argentina on Sunday night

It was a devastating end for Lionel Messi though who has likely played his last World Cup game

Spain (4-2-3-1)

Unai Simon - 6

Twice off his line in a flash to clear after balls were dropped in behind for Messi and Alvarez to chase. But there was not a save to make.

Pedro Porro - 6

Hardly troubled in defence so took that opportunity to join attack, as he likes to. Heavily involved, - more than 120 touches - but crosses rarely found intended target.

Pau Cubarsi - 8

Tried to get his team going with forward passes from deep, including one to get Yamal away. Was super cool in defence, too. He’s a star.

Aymeric Laporte - 7

Rarely flustered at the back so subdued was Messi and thought he’d won it with late header plucked on goal-line by Martinez.

Marc Cucurella - 7

Typically snappy in his challenges and, like Porro, poured forward when realising how passive Argentina were. Nearly scored opener with low drill wide.

Rodri - 7

Imperious early on and everything went through him. He looked like the grown-up in midfield battle. That influence faded and he could not find the pass to break stubborn Argentina.

Rodri dictated the game for Spain in midfield and ended up winning Player of the Tournament

Pau Cubarsi was brilliant in defence and helped start Spain's attacks with his superb passing

Fabian Ruiz - 6

A threat amid otherwise mundane first half, but way below best. Came into it more after break and dribble led to good chance for Torres. Much like whole tournament, not the final we’d hoped for from him.

Lamine Yamal - 7

A threat amid otherwise mundane first half, but still below best. Came into it more after break and dribble led to good chance for Torres. Much like whole tournament, not really the final we’d hoped for from him, but played his part.

Dani Olmo - 6

Like many of Spain’s other attacking starters he just could not produce that moment of inspiration. Not as peripheral as the others, but no real impact.

Alex Baena - 4

No end product from left wing and was a surprise he stayed on until 75th minute. A big chance to impress but Atletico Madrid man did not take it.

Mikel Oyarzabal - 5

A star of the tournament but this was a game to forget on the biggest occasion. One shot on target and one touch in area before making way just after hour.

Mikel Oyarzabal has been one of the stars of the tournament but didn't enjoy his best game

Lamine Yamal was a threat throughout the match but the wonderkid was still below his best

Substitutes

Ferran Torres (on for Oyarzabal 62) - 8

Pedri (on for Fabian Ruiz 62) - 7

Mikel Merino (on for Olmo 75) - 6

Nico Williams (on for Baena 75) - 9

Martin Zubimendi (on for Rodri 99) - 6

Eric Garcia (on for Laporte 99) - 6

Manager: Luis de la Fuente - 8

Has now delivered the World Cup and European Championship. They made hard work of this and should have been good enough to win in normal time, but the introduction of Williams and Torres was the inspiration Spain needed.

Ferran Torres came off the bench to score Spain's winner and write himself into Spain's history

Argentina (4-4-2)

Emiliano Martinez - 8

Improvised early on to deny Yamal and that was the first of 11 saves. Kept his team in the game and had no chance with winner. Easily Argentina’s best.

Gonzalo Montiel - 6

Saved likely goal when stealing from toe of Cucurella in penalty area after half-time, but that was his last involvement. Had been solid before that.

Cristian Romero - 6

Never far from the action, as is his way, and got the better of Oyarzabal in duel with Spain’s five-goal striker. Seemed to tire after exertions of semi versus England.

Lisandro Martinez - 5

Injury nightmare just before half-time when hurting his thigh as he brought down Rodri. Long balls had been wasteful to that point.

Lisandro Martinez suffered an injury nightmare and was forced off before half-time

Emiliano Martinez kept his team in the game and ended up making 11 saves in total

Nicolas Tagliafico - 7

Tasked with keeping Yamal quiet and, one or two flashes from the Spain winger apart, it was a job he did well. Emerges with credit.

Rodrigo De Paul - 5

His loose pass caused team-mate Lisandro to foul Rodri at expense of booking and injury. Was diligent in defensive work but not good enough on the ball.

Alexis Mac Allister - 4

Shocking first half. Repeatedly found red with stray passes and was lucky to escape yellow for lunge on Olmo. Recovered to put in decent shift but quality still lacking.

Enzo Fernandez - 3

Red card shame on back of untidy display. He set the tone against England but was too passive here, except when committing the two second-half fouls that brought deserved yellows.

Nico Gonzalez - 3

Anonymous and invariably lost the ball when he did get it. Was no surprise to see him hooked at the break after completing only five passes.

Lionel Messi - 5

One touch first 15 minutes and that was from kick off. Also pulled out of 50-50 with Simon. Justin Bieber got closer to the penalty area in normal time. Belatedly came to life in final moments and was dangerous. All too late, though.

Lionel Messi was left heartbroken after enduring a quiet game as he struggled to get involved

Enzo Fernandez is the sixth player to be sent off during a World Cup final and let his side down

Julian Alvarez - 4

Tried to do the running while Messi walked but had no service and left the field after 102 minutes without a shot. You could sense his frustration.

Substitutes

Nicolas Otamendi (on for L Martinez 45) 6

Leandro Paredes (on for Gonzalez 46) 4

Nahuel Molina (on for Montiel 58) 5

Giuliano Simeone (on for De Paul 70) 5

Facundo Medina (on for Romero 70) 5

Marcos Senesi (on for Alvarez 102) 5

Manager: Lionel Scaloni - 4

Didn't send out his team with same snarliness as against England and, come the end, they had not even found the target over 120 minutes. A weak defence of their title.

Referee: Slavko Vincic - 5

Sports.title: World Cup final descends into violence at full-time whistle as Spain and Argentina players clash in ugly scenes
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The World Cup final descended into outrageous scenes as fights broke out among the two sets of players.

Some of Argentina's players lost their heads as Spain's substitutes and staff ran on to the pitch to celebrate their 1-0 win against the South Americans.

Ferran Torres scored a 106th-minute winner after Enzo Fernandez had been sent off in the 93rd minute for a desperately poor Argentina side.

After the whistle, Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes was sent off for punching Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground.

Argentina's Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso as he was running by, while Thiago Almada was involved, too.

Micah Richards said of their behaviour on the BBC: 'It's embarrassing. They were on the cusp every single time.

'Seeing that sort of stuff after the game was played, it's not good, it's embarrassing to be honest. Paredes is better than that. We all know what it's like to lose a game but this is not good enough.'

Argentina's Leandro Paredes was sent off after the whistle for getting violent with Spain

Several stars clashed after Spain's 1-0 win over Argentina - but the South Americans started it

Joe Hart added: 'Disgusting behaviour. There was one man on that pitch with class and that was Lionel Messi.'

Wayne Rooney said: 'It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this from Argentina before. It's just sad, very poor from them.

'If you lose a game of football, be graceful. It's a reaction to them being outplayed. Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves.'

Argentina were thuggish throughout the World Cup final, just as they had been against England in the semis.

Fernandez complained against his dismissal for a second yellow but his late foul on Pau Cubarsi, which sent the defender flying, was atrocious.

Paredes was also fortunate to not be sent off in regular time for a foul on the edge of the box which presented Lamine Yamal with a last-breath free-kick before extra-time.

Argentina only had two shots in the entire match, and the first of those came in the 117th minute.

By contrast, they were trigger-happy on the fouls with 24 - though Spain didn't have clean hands themselves, as they gave away 21.

Paredes was blasted for getting violent at full time and trying to ruin Spain's celebrations

Alan Shearer said: 'There's a way to lose. Too many times we've seen that reaction from them. They were trying to win free-kicks and their reaction after full time was terrible. The best team won. It's a result for football because of the way Spain have played.'

Even Lionel Messi didn't rise above the dark arts. The legendary forward was lambasted by Wayne Rooney after he tried to get Marc Cucurella sent off during the latter stages of the game.

The game descended into chaos when Fernandez received his second yellow card.

This led to a melee between both sets of players and Cucurella was spotted saying something to Messi.

The left-back then put a couple of fingers over his mouth and continued speaking, a move which the Argentine immediately reacted to and waved over the referee.

As per FIFA's rules for this tournament, if a player holds their hand over their mouth in a confrontational situation, they will be sent off.

This was seen with Miguel Almiron for Paraguay in the group stage and Piero Hincapie in the knockout stages for Ecuador.

However, it didn't appear that Cucurella was speaking in a confrontational manner and the referee, nor VAR, decided to intervene.

Spain have won the World Cup after Ferran Torres' extra-time winner against Argentina

Torres smashed in the goal with his left foot after Williams headed the ball back across goal

It was elation for the Spanish players as they celebrated wildly in the corner of the stadium

But it was devastation for Argentina's crestfallen stars, who had fought for their lives

There was no fairytale World Cup ending for Lionel Messi who struggled to assert his authority

The BBC pundits were quick to hit out at Messi's behaviour as his team headed into extra time a man down.

Hart said: 'Oh wow! Wow! Yeah, I didn't enjoy that at all from Lionel Messi.

'You realise how on top Spain are if even Lionel Messi is reverting to that.'

Richards added: 'We don't want to see people getting sent off in a World Cup final for that.'

Rooney was similarly furious with Messi's behaviour as he said: 'It is desperation.

'Argentina play like that, we know that's what they do.

'But the one thing you want is good sportsmanship and that was sad to see Lionel Messi doing that.'

Sports.title: Spain vs Argentina player ratings as Enzo Fernandez costs his side the World Cup final
Sports.content:
Spain have won the World Cup for the second time after beating a dour Argentina side 1-0 after extra time in the final.

After the pageantry before kick-off, the first half was an extremely cagey affair with Lamine Yamal going closest. Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez then suffered heartache shortly before the break when he was forced off with an injury.

Both sides then had to sit in their respective dressing room for a relative eternity as the World Cup final was paused for the much-feted half-time show.

It was much of the same once they did appear though, with Spain dominating possession but failing to carve out any gilt-edge chances.

‌



As extra time loomed, Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez was shown red after flying into a tackle already on a yellow card.

‌

Sports.title: World Cup final ends in chaos as Argentina star throws punches after Spain win
Sports.content:
World Cup final ends in chaos as Argentina star throws punches after Spain win

Punches were thrown at full time of the World Cup final after Spain defeated Argentina thanks to Ferran Torres' goal in extra time at MetLife Stadium

View 3 Images Players clashed after Spain beat Argentina in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final in the USA

Spain's World Cup win over Argentina was marred by unsavoury scenes at the full-time whistle, with punches thrown. Leandro Paredes was sent off following the whistle, while Molina also appeared to throw a punch after the match.

‌



The latter took a swing at Rodri, while Paredes was spotted kicking Eric Garcia to the floor before pushing him back with a hand around his neck when the Barcelona defender attempted to confront him. He was also spotted in an exchange with Gavi.

‌



Chaos reigned as Spain begain their jubilant celebrations elsewhere on the pitch.

‌



"Paredes threw two or three haymakers into someone's face. He went for them," said Alan Shearer. "There is no place or space for that.

"We know how much it means to them and we know how much it hurts to lose, but there is a way to lose. Too many times we have seen that from Argentina. The reaction after the final whistle is terrible."

Lionel Messi slammed for desperate attempt to get Spain star sent off in World Cup final READ MORE :

World Cup fans issue the same complaint about half-time show as Spain vs Argentina delayed READ MORE :

Gary Neville had a simple assessment. "I love the competitiveness of the Argentines but Paredes has been a disgrace the last couple of games," he said.

‌



Wayne Rooney was not surprised by how Argentina handled the defeat. He said: "Does is surprise you? It doesn't surprise me, I think we've seen this with Argentina before and it's just not the reaction you want.

"We've seen some of the reaction after knocking England out in the last round as well. I think Enzo Fernandez has got what he deserves as well, so it's disappointing. But that's just sad. If you lose a game of football, be graceful and get out of there. It's very poor from them."

View 3 Images The World Cup final ended in chaotic scenes (Image: TV)

‌



Ex-England goalkeeper Joe Hart added: "Disgusting. There was one man on the pitch who did have class, and that was Lionel Mess - shook hands of every one of those Spanish players.

"The game's done, they can have absolutely no complaints about what happened today. Disgusting behaviour.

"Rodri, I don't think, needed to get in their faces, but when you've been wound up for 120 minutes, and you felt you've been wronged, and you've felt the referee's on your back, and you've got that win, referee's blown his whistle, leave it. And I think Argentina...are you surprised they've gone over the line again?"

‌



Micah Richards ensured that the pundits were unanimous in their assessment. He said: "The first yellow card wasn't until 40 odd minutes in the first-half, but seeing that sort of stuff after the game's been played and someone's just been crowned World Cup champions, it's not good enough.

View 3 Images Leandro Paredes and Eric Garcia have words after the FIFA World Cup 2026 final (Image: Al Bello/Getty Images)

"It's quite embarrassing to be honest. Paraedes there, he doesn't need to do that, he's better than that.

‌



"And it doesn't stop there, it keeps going, and going, and going. And we all know what it's like to lose a game, we can be very frustrated, we understand that. But this is not good enough, it's not a good look at all."

The fiery end followed a game where Paredes was lucky to stay on the pitch, despite only entering the field at half-time. The Argentina star was lucky to stay on the field after a number of questionable challenges.

The World Cup runners-up saw Enzo Fernandez sent off in the 93rd minute of the match, leaving them with a one-man disadvantage heading into extra time. A tense tie was eventually separated by Ferran Torres as the European team became world champions for the first time since 2010.

Sports.title: Spain beat Argentina in World Cup final after Enzo Fernandez's moment of madness - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Ferran Torres was in the right place at the right time to mercifully settle a drab World Cup final in extra-time as Spain's dominance finally told against Argentina in New Jersey.

The reigning world champions, chasing history as they sought to become just the third team to ever win successive World Cups, failed to show up. Even with the genius of Lionel Messi in tow, Argentina were toothless on the biggest stage, failing to muster a single shot on goal until the 117th minute.

An uneventful first half slowly turned into a lulling Spain siege with Emi Martinez called into action to thwart Dani Olmo. It was the Aston Villa star keeping Argentina alive, making saves from Torres, Aymeric Laporte and numerous others as Spain increased the pressure.

Then, with extra-time looming, Enzo Fernandez was shown a second yellow card after the Chelsea midfielder went flying into Pau Cubarsi in a 50-50 near halfway to leave Argentina with a mountain to climb.

‌



Spain thought they finally had the goal their play merited in the early minutes of extra-time when Nico Williams smuggled the ball into the back of the net through a sea of bodies in the box before it was chalked off. But Argentina and Martinez's resistance was finally broken in the 106th minute when Torres plundered the winning goal.

Here are Mirror Football's talking points from the World Cup final...

World Cup final LIVE: Spain vs Argentina match and goal updates as Martinez suffers injury blow READ MORE :

Lisandro Martinez in floods of tears as Man Utd star suffers World Cup final agony READ MORE :

1. Argentina's fortune continues...until it doesn't

Unless you've been living under a rock for the last month, you'll probably be aware that Argentina have benefitted from some favourable officiating decisions. Egypt, eliminated in the most heartbreaking yet epic fashion by the defending world champions in the round of 16, even alleged there was a bias towards Lionel Scaloni's side from Fifa.

There were more than a few circumstances during the England-Argentina game where those in blue and white stripes were fortunate to avoid being reprimanded by the officials. And wherever you stand on such talk, Alexis Mac Allister escaping punishment for a late, reckless challenge on Dani Olmo early in the first half will do little to stifle such accusations.

‌



Maybe Argentina have just had the rub of the green on their way to tonight's final. But more than a few incidents during their enthralling run to the final, including Mac Allister's escape and the decision to rule out a Williams goal in extra-time for a soft foul on Nico Otamendi, have left an extremely sour taste.

2. A slow burn

View 5 Images Alexis Mac Allister was fortunate to escape punishment for a reckless challenge on Dani Olmo (Image: Daniela Porcelli)

Pre-match, the big question on the BBC's coverage of the final was over who would be the unfortunate soul to follow Jennifer Hudson and her epic performance of the American national anthem. But perhaps the real concern should have been over this match following the 10-goal thriller England and France served up in their bronze final less than 24 hours earlier.

Alright, the occasion isn't comparable and nerves and tension will have undoubtedly played a part in a drab first half, which saw the fewest shots (three, all for Spain) in any half of a World Cup final in history.

‌



For all the razzmatazz of the United States' big plans for its pre-match coverage, not to mention a half-time show, the action on the pitch didn't live up to the billing here. Even with an additional half an hour of play.

3. Fernandez's moment of madness

View 5 Images Enzo Fernandez was sent off in the final minutes of normal time

Not even Argentina and their good fortune could survive Fernandez and his stupid decision to go absolutely hurtling into Cubarsi in the final moments of extra-time. Already on a yellow card for dissent, there could only be one outcome.

Considering Argentina were pretty much under the pump for the whole game, Fernandez's cheap dismissal felt like the death knell for their chances of becoming just the third nation in history to win successive World Cups.

‌



Fernandez was distraught, but it was an absolute moment of madness from a player who rescued Argentina in their hour of need just days beforehand. If Fernandez saved Argentina's World Cup hopes with his stunner against England, then he absolutely killed them here.

4. Martinez's one-man stand v Spain

View 5 Images Emi Martinez kept Argentina alive in the World Cup final with save after save (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer/GES Sportfoto)

Spain dominated the game in regulation time when both sides had 11 men, so there was an air of inevitably about Spain's winning goal when it eventually did come in extra-time. But if one man on the pitch didn't deserve to be on the losing side, it was Martinez.

Heroic in Qatar four years ago as Argentina bested France on penalties, Martinez produced a performance on par with that in New Jersey, even if it was not enough to lift his country to yet more history.

‌



After springing to the turf to repel another Spain attempt, Martinez turned to whip up the crowd shortly after Fernandez's dismissal. But even Argentina's larger than life keeper was unable to deny Torres' powerful effort, Martinez finally beaten at the 12th attempt.

5. The Messi-Yamal final falls flat

View 5 Images Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal faced off in New Jersey (Image: Alex Livesey/Danehouse)

We've all seen the picture; that one of Messi crading a baby Yamal taken when the Argentine magician was a teenager with the world at his feet. This was the dream final that Fifa would have privately craved months ago: the one that pitted master vs apprentice, Messi against Yamal. Narrative wise, it was pitch-perfect.

Unfortunately, it transpired to be anything but. Both were ineffective and bystanders for large periods as Spain and Argentina sparred nervously for more than two hours.

‌



This has been a tournament where Messi, even at 39 years of age, has cemented has reputation as the world's undisputed best, orchestrating resurrections against Cape Verde, Egypt and England to propel Argentina to a second successive World Cup final. But their tournament ended with a whimper here; Argentina were practically non-existent as an attacking force, failing to muster a single attempt on goal in regulation time. This was a meek surrender.

In the case of Yamal, there were flashes of the genius that will almost certainly ensure he enjoys a long, fruitful reign as one of football's new icons. But like Messi, he too was on the periphery for much of this final. In truth, it's been that sort of tournament for Messi's Barcelona heir.

This World Cup will be remembered for many things. Unfortunately, the Messi-Yamal final will not be one of them.

Sports.content:
World Cup Golden Boot winner confirmed after Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi battle

The race for the 2026 World Cup Golden Boot has been decided as Spain secured a 1-0 win over Argentina in Sunday's grand final in New Jersey

View Image Kylian Mbappe won the 2026 World Cup Golden Boot (Image: Europa Press via Getty Images)

Kylian Mbappe has won the race for the 2026 World Cup Golden Boot, finishing the competition on 10 goals after a stellar tournament in North America. That's despite Lionel Messi having a major advantage in the opportunity to bolster his own tally of eight during Sunday's final against Spain.

‌



The 39-year-old was unable to do so, however, with his nation suffering heartbreak at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey in the form of a 1-0 loss in extra-time. Ferran Torres broke the deadlock for the European champions 106 minutes into play, not only to give his nation the lead, but ultimately win the match.

‌



It was a remarkable tournament for Mbappe, who proved himself once more on the world stage in North America. The 27-year-old kickstarted his tournament with a boom last month, bagging a brace in a 3-1 opening day win with France against Senegal.

Another goal from the penalty spot came during France's 1-0 win over Paraguay in the round of 16, while another from open play came during their 2-0 quarter-final win against Morocco. Sports.title: Spain overwhelm dismal Argentina to win the World Cup for second time
Sports.content:
Finally justice was done in the MetLife Stadium.

The one team who came to play football won against the kings of anti-football.

Ferran Torres was Spain’s hero even if it needed extra time to see off Lionel Messi and Co as holders Argentina lost their grip on the World Cup trophy.

Messi’s dreams were left in tatters as this did not feel a remotely fitting way for one of football’s greatest players of all time to bow out if this proves to be his final act for his country.

‌



Argentina were dreadful, they did not manage a single shot on target and it felt as if they had no ambition to win the game. Enzo Fernandez was sent off in injury time at the end of 90 minutes and that just about summed up their ugly, spoiling and nasty approach.

And Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes greeted the final whistle by sparking a melee and swinging punches at celebrating Spain stars.

Wayne Rooney leaves BBC pundits speechless with brutal review of World Cup half-time show READ MORE :

Donald Trump brutally booed at World Cup final as Spain and Argentina fans unite READ MORE :

In contrast, Spain ushered in a new world order as the European champions now rule the world and they were utterly dominant in a final which did not really live up to its billing.

They thoroughly deserved their win and their stylish football helped us focus on the pitch and forget the silly showbiz that FIFA tried to impose on their showcase game.

‌



Spain had so many chances, so many near misses and Emiliano Martinez was Argentina’s hero with an incredible performance as he produced at least a dozen saves.

That is the one flaw in Spain’s make-up - they do not have a goal poacher who can finish off their wonderful, free-flowing approach play.

It needed a flick on from Nico Williams to set up Torres to finally seal the victory which sparked wild scenes of celebrations among the sea of red shirts in the crowd.

This was their day and a victory for football over spoilers but also helped the purists savour the game and quickly forget about lavish pre-match and half time shows.

‌



View 4 Images Lionel Messi during the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina

They had music, light shows and a bizarre half set which left most of the crowd cold amid the blazing sun in New Jersey.

The true football fans had come for the game and Argentina had just run out of dirty tricks, energy and legs after their exertions against England.

Mind you, Thomas Tuchel’s men must have been watching on from holiday and be thinking they would have given a better account of themselves than Argentina.

‌



They were woeful. Never looked like retaining their trophy - they wanted to become the first team since Brazil in 1962 to do that - and they looked a spent force.

View 4 Images Spain are champions of the world for the second time

Spain were bright, dominant and Rodri conducted them from midfield as they created chance after chance but were thwarted by Martinez.

Lamine Yamal did not really step up but had a good game and yet they just could not score. Lisandro Martinez went off injured for Argentina and they became the walking wounded after so many comebacks in this World Cup.

‌



Pedri, Torres and Mikel Merino all went close while Williams had an effort ruled out as you began to wonder whether they would score.

Even after Fernandez’s red card - for a second yellow after a foul on Pau Cubarsí - did not help Spain as Argentina dug in to try and hold on for penalties.

View 4 Images Enzo Fernandez was shown a red card in the closing stages of normal time

It felt like it was heading that way until Torres’ intervention. Then - and only then - did we see signs of life from Argentina.

‌



They pushed, Messi tried and they went close but Spain were superior and deserved their win.

This Argentina side looked to have reached the end of the road. Too many ageing players. Surely Messi will call it quits at 39 or he will certainly retire before the next World Cup.

Mentality and fight has carried them a long way in this tournament - and that is to be admired. If only England had as much.

But they were undone by a much better footballing side and Spain are now kings of the world again. And deservedly so.

‌

Sports.title: Lionel Messi slammed for desperate attempt to get Spain star sent off in World Cup final
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi slammed for desperate attempt to get Spain star sent off in World Cup final

Enzo Fernandez was sent off for Argentina during stoppage time in their World Cup final clash with Spain, but Lionel Messi also tried to get a Spain star red carded during the clash

View Image Lionel Messi tried to get Marc Cucurella sent off during the World Cup final (Image: BBC)

Lionel Messi was slammed by Wayne Rooney, Micah Richards and Joe Hart for trying to get Marc Cucurella sent off in sly fashion during the World Cup final. A moment of excitement sparked late into Argentina's clash with Spain at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, following a largely lacklustre 90 minutes, when Enzo Fernandez was given an early exit.

‌



The Chelsea star, who was already on a yellow for dissent earlier in the match, bundled through Pau Curbasi needlessly during stoppage time, sending him feet into the air with a dangling leg and leaving him in a heap on the floor. Referee Slavko Vincic didn't hesitate as he showed Fernandez a red card for the cynical foul, with immediate protests from the 25-year-old.

‌



However, it was during the furore that Messi attempted to immediately level the playing field by getting Cucurella sent off. Replays showed the Real Madrid full-back somewhat raising his hand to his face as he conversed with the Argentine captain.

‌



Donald Trump picks his World Cup winner and makes request to Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

Alan Shearer lets rip at 'stupid' Enzo Fernandez sent off in Spain vs Argentina World Cup final READ MORE :

While his mouth wasn't fully covered, a new rule from FIFA in a bid to rub out racism has been implemented for this summer's tournament, which prevents players from speaking to opponents with their mouths covered.

And while Cucurella may not have said anything sinister as he conversed with the 39-year-old, Messi was quick to flag to officials that Cucurella had covered his mouth.

The forward's pleas ultimately fell on deaf ears, however, as no action was taken against Cucurella.

‌



And as the two sides headed into extra time, the BBC panel of Rooney, Richards, Hart and Gabby Logan voiced their frustrations with the showing from one of the world's most respected players.

Logan said: "And of course there was a moment with Messi and Cucarella where he was trying to potentially get him sent off here. Cucarella has talked behind his hand, or Messi has said he has, and Messi immediately calls an official. Micah, what do you make of that?"

‌



Shocked by the move, Richards replied: "He's not got his whole hand over, he's got two fingers. It's harsh isn't it? You don't want to see people getting sent off in a World Cup final for that."

Hart then gave his two cents as he added: "Yeah, I didn't enjoy that at all.

"You realise how on top Spain are in this game if even Lionel Messi is reverting to that," before Logan replied: "Desperation from Messi there?"

Sports.title: Alan Shearer lets rip at 'stupid' Enzo Fernandez sent off in Spain vs Argentina World Cup final
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer lets rip at 'stupid' Enzo Fernandez sent off in Spain vs Argentina World Cup final

Alan Shearer did not hold back with his verdict of Enzo Fernandez's red card in the World Cup final

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez was shown a red card for a reckless challenge in the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina (Image: BBC Sport)

Alan Shearer ripped into Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernadez after he was sent off in the World Cup final clash with Spain. The Chelsea star had been shown a yellow card midway through the first half for dissent toward the match officials, before being shown a second yellow for a reckless foul on Pau Cubarsi just minutes before the final whistle.

‌



The game was edging toward extra-time when the 25-year-old went flying into a tackle on the halfway line, with Spain posing no real danger to his side. Cubarsi beat Fernandez to the ball, but the Argentinian midfielder made sure he left his mark on his opponent, upending the Spanish defender.

‌



Referee Slavko Vincic wasted no time in showing Fernandez a second yellow, but the Argentinian midfielder still remonstrated with the officials.

‌



Wayne Rooney leaves BBC pundits speechless with brutal review of World Cup half-time show READ MORE :

Lisandro Martinez in floods of tears as Man Utd star suffers World Cup final agony READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Lionel Messi and Fernandez were both seen arguing with the officials, appearing to call for Marc Cucurella to be shown a red card for covering his mouth with his hand after the original red card incident.

Nothing was given and the Argentinian midfielder was handed his marching orders.

‌



Speaking on co-commentary, Shearer said: "He might just have cost his team massively, because you know now that Argentina are going to try to take it to penalties. With him already being on a yellow card for something stupid - backchatting to the referee.

"And when you're on a yellow, you cannot, cannot make a challenge like that. That is stupid from him, it really is.

"I mean how daft is that from Enzo Fernandez? He's on a yellow card for dissent. Not for the tackel, for dissent. And he knows that, because that didn't happen long ago.

‌



"So for him to go into a challenge like that is crazy. He can protest as much as he wants, but it's the right decision. Gave the referee only one choice, and that was to issue another yellow - therefore the red."

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez was slammed by Alan Shearer after being shown a red card in the World Cup final clash against Spain. (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Wayne Rooney also gave a brutal verdict on the red card ahead of extra-time and said: "It's just a silly tackle. I think he's obviously a little bit late to it as we see here, and on a yellow card you can't just dangle your leg out and give the opposition an opportunity to get you a red card.

‌



"It's silly from Fernandez and it makes it a very different game now for Argentina to get through extra-time. Spain were on top as it was, but this makes it even more difficult."

Argentina did not register a single shot on goal inside the 90 minutes, even with 11 men on the pitch and managed just one touch inside the Spanish box.

Spain were the dominant side with 15 shots, ten of which were on target and 23 touches inside the opposition box, but weren't able to find a way past Emi Martinez as the game went into extra-time.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney leaves BBC pundits speechless with brutal review of World Cup half-time show
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney leaves BBC pundits speechless with brutal review of World Cup half-time show

Wayne Rooney made his feelings about the World Cup half-time show crystal clear

View Image Wayne Rooney was left furious (Image: BBC Sport)

Manchester United and England legend Wayne Rooney branded the World Cup final half-time show 'crap' in a brutally honest verdict. The opening 45 minutes of Argentina and Spain ended 0-0 with the European champions the better of the two sides at the break before a star-studded cast took to the pitch.

‌



The World Cup final has already come under major scrutiny with the pre-match show delaying kick-off by six minutes. While Donald Trump's appearance at the Met Life Stadium caused major delays for fans and members of the media getting into the ground due to heightened security measures.

‌



Spain were the more attacking of the two sides, with Argentina failing to register a single shot in the opening 45 minutes, while the European champions went close through Lamine Yamal and Mikel Oyarzabal.

‌



Donald Trump brutally booed at World Cup final as Spain and Argentina fans unite READ MORE :

When the half-time whistle blew, players quickly left the field of play and it was a huge 27 minutes and 18 seconds until they returned, with the half-time show taking place.

As per the International Football Association Board rules, the half-time break should be no longer than 15 minutes, with the interval in breach of those rules.

‌



Justin Bieber, Madonna, Shakira, Gustavo Dudamel and BTS all performed in the half-time show, which was curated by Chris Martin from Coldplay. However, Rooney wasn't impressed.

Speaking on the BBC, Rooney said: "I'll be honest, mine (highlight) was when it finished. I like lot of those artists but I thought it was crap.

"I did, honestly. It just didn't get me going. I want the football to come back on. I like Burna Boy, I like Bieber, I like Shakira. That was flat."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Micah Richards, who picked the performances of Shakira and Burna Boy as his highlights, called former international team-mate Rooney “miserable” for his frank assessment.

With the conversation following an advert promoting the BBC, host Gabby Logan added: “I’ll tell you what else you get on the BBC: honest reviews”.

‌



FIFA president Gianni Infantino announced plans for the show – which was curated by Coldplay frontman Chris Martin – in March last year.

Fans were left shocked to see Madonna arrive into the stadium on a buggy with Brazilian legends Ronaldo and Ronaldinho driving the cart.

One fan said: "Madonna, Ronaldo the Phenomenon, and Ronaldinho Gaúcho together - never thought I'd see this."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
