The Atomic Energy Organization of Iran said the United States had attacked the unfinished Darkhovin nuclear power plant in the country’s southwest, calling it \”an aggressive and brutal act contrary to international law\”.

The UN’s nuclear watchdog said it was looking into the report, noting the plant \”contained no nuclear material when last visited by the IAEA\”.

Nonetheless, IAEA director Rafael Grossi reiterated his \”call for military restraint in the vicinity of all nuclear-related sites\”, the agency said in a post on X.

Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi meanwhile said on X that Tehran \”will take appropriate action to defend its national interests and security.\”

– ‘Treacherous’ attacks –

After air raid sirens sounded in Jordan, Israel’s military said its forces along with Jordan’s had intercepted an Iranian missile heading towards the Jordanian port city of Aqaba — just across the border from Israel’s resort town of Eilat.

Iran did not immediately claim the attack, but the US embassy in Amman had earlier warned its citizens of a \”specific and credible threat\” targeting Aqaba’s port and airport.

\”If Iran fires missiles at Israel, we will attack them with full force,\” Defence Minister Israel Katz said, adding it was \”prepared for both defensive and offensive\” action against Tehran if need be.

Jordan later said it had summoned Iran’s charge d’affaires to strongly protest the \”continuation of brutal and unjustified Iranian acts of aggression targeting the Kingdom’s territory\”.

In the Gulf, which has borne the brunt of Iran’s retaliatory attacks, Kuwait’s electricity ministry said a power and water plant was attacked for a second consecutive day, causing a fire.

Bahrain’s military also said its air defences \”confronted, intercepted, and destroyed a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks\”, accusing Iran of targeting civilians.

– American ‘mischief’ –

The renewed violence was initially sparked by Iranian attacks on ships in the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

Iran closed the conduit for oil and gas shipments after the war broke out, and control over it has become leverage in its negotiations with Washington, which has reimposed its own blockade on Iranian ports.

On Sunday, the Revolutionary Guards said two ships attempting to transit the strait were stopped.

\”Four violating ships, with the mischief and support of American terrorists…intended to disrupt and exit the Strait of Hormuz via an unsafe route, two of which had an accident and were stopped in place,\” the Guards said, adding that the other two ships abandoned their journey.

Iran’s health ministry said Friday that 50 people had been killed in the recent fighting and more than 500 hurt.

Hope for a political settlement to the war has dimmed, though mediators have attempted to bring both sides back to the negotiating table.

Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who took over after his father was killed in the opening salvo of US-Israeli strikes, vowed to teach the Americans \”unforgettable lessons\” in a statement Saturday.

And Iran’s central military commander, Ali Abdollahi, warned that further US aggression would face a \”decisive and devastating response\”, according to a statement carried by state television on Sunday.

World.title: Madonna, Shakira, Bieber and The Muppets light up World Cup half-time show
World.content:
East Rutherford – Musical headliners Madonna, Shakira, Justin Bieber, BTS and Coldplay were joined by Brazilian soccer icons and \”Ted Lasso\” actors in a spectacular first-ever World Cup final halftime show on Sunday.

The star-packed, Super Bowl-style extravaganza — a first for soccer’s showpiece event — also featured a tribute to football icon Pele, and a rendition of \”Seven Nation Army\” led by Gustavo Dudamel and featuring musicians from the US, Venezuela and Iran.

\”Sesame Street\” and \”The Muppets\” characters joined Coldplay and a New York elementary school choir to close out a performance designed to raise money for the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, which promotes access to sport for under-privileged children.

The 12-minute performance meant the total halftime break in the match between Spain and Argentina lasted 27 minutes.

– Largest since Live Aid? –

Organizers had billed the halftime show as \”the single largest gathering of artists united for a cause since Live Aid,\” and \”the most-watched 11 minutes of broadcast music performance in history\”.

FIFA chief Gianni Infantino predicted \”a couple of billion\” people would tune in.

The extended interruption to soccer’s most important game had drawn some criticism over the potential impact on players’ performance.

While highly unusual for soccer, the show was slightly shorter than most recent Super Bowl halftime performances, which have typically been around 13-14 minutes long.

The crowd erupted with a roar as the show began with Madonna being transported through tunnels beneath the MetLife Stadium on a dune buggy driven by Brazil soccer legends Ronaldo and Ronaldinho.

Her performance of \”Music\” led to an orchestra featuring the New York Philharmonic, Venezuela’s Simon Bolivar Symphony Orchestra and Iranian violinist Bijan Mortazavi performing the White Stripes’ \”Seven Nation Army\” — a rock hit that has become a global US soccer stadium staple.

Footage of the Norway fans’ \”Viking row\” celebration from this tournament led into K-pop sensation BTS performing their smash hit \”Dynamite,\” rewritten with soccer-specific lyrics, before \”Ted Lasso\” star Jason Sudeikis and his \”Coach Beard\” sidekick Brendan Hunt made a surprise appearance.

They introduced Canadian pop megastar Bieber, who performed an emotional, World Cup-tailored version of \”Everything Hallelujah,\” before Shakira and Nigerian singer Burna Boy ramped the energy back up with this World Cup’s anthem, \”Dai Dai,\” accompanied by Ugandan dancers.

– ‘Driving force’ –

Ggiant screens showed footage of Brazil’s late soccer icon Pele from 1977, addressing the crowd at the old Giants Stadium on this same New Jersey site following his final professional game. Pele passed away in 2022, months after the last World Cup.

PS22 Chorus, a New York school choir that has gone viral globally with YouTube covers of popular hits, closed out the show, with Coldplay — whose singer Chris Martin curated the entire performance — and characters from \”The Muppets\” and \”Sesame Street.\”

The FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund was described by organizers as the \”driving force\” behind the halftime show.

It disburses cash to community groups that provide education and sport to under-priviliged children in countries from Ghana and South Africa to France and the United Kingdom.

The fund aims to raise $100 million. It had passed $60 million before the show, including a $1 donation from every World Cup ticket sold, plus contributions from corporations, nation states and private donors.

FIFA has already announced 58 groups that will receive grants, reaching 400,000 children worldwide.

Even before the game, a parade of stars took the microphone to whip up the crowd.

Post Malone headlined a closing ceremony, and Tom Cruise delivered a monologue about football unifying the world — but was largely drowned out in the stadium by singing fans.

Robbie Williams, Nicole Scherzinger and Jennifer Hudson were among further A-list performers.

World.title: US soldier killed in Iraq while dismantling Iranian attack drone
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com)—A US service member was killed and another injured in northern Iraq while disposing of explosive ordnance from a crashed Iranian one-way attack drone, the US military announced on Sunday.

The soldier was killed on July 18 during a controlled explosion of unexploded explosives from the drone, while the second service member had a minor injury and is being treated, according to US Central Command (CENTCOM).

The event occurs as Iraq strives to convince international investors that improved security and economic reforms are rebuilding trust after decades of strife, despite regional tensions spilling into Iraqi territory.

During a recent visit to Washington, Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s government signed a series of agreements with US companies and financial institutions on energy, infrastructure, aviation, and banking as part of Baghdad’s larger effort to diversify its economy and attract foreign investment.

The latest incident highlights the security threats that continue to impede Iraq’s recovery, with strikes utilizing Iranian drones and Iran-backed armed groups disturbing peace, resulting in lives and injuries, and threatening to dissuade foreign investment.

Separately, CENTCOM said that two US service members died as a result of an Iranian strike in Jordan on July 17 and that military troops subsequently discovered unidentifiable remains suspected to be those of a third service member who had been reported missing.

An investigation to confirm the remains is continuing.

CENTCOM said that it was concealing the identity of the deceased and missing service men out of respect for their families until the notification procedure was completed.

Following years of conflict, Iraq has increasingly sought to position itself as a stable destination for international business.

However, recurring regional hostilities have repeatedly exposed the country’s vulnerability to broader tensions between Iran and the United States, complicating Baghdad’s efforts to restore normalcy and sustain its economic recovery.

World.title: PM Al Zaidi carries Trump message to Iran; Tehran declines Supreme Leader meeting
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Well-informed sources have disclosed to the Kuwaiti newspaper Al-Jarida, that Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi is carrying a verbal message from U.S. President Donald Trump addressed to the Iranian leadership. This message, which al-Zaidi received during his recent official visit to Washington, comes as the U.S.–Iran confrontation edges closer to a broader war amid ongoing regional military escalation.

The sources from the Iranian Supreme National Security Council explained that the Iraqi Prime Minister’s stopover in the Qatari capital of Doha on Sunday was specifically aimed at coordinating the core substance of this message with the Qatari side. Baghdad is seeking to evaluate the possibility of transforming this verbal message into a tangible Iraqi initiative that works in tandem with current mediation tracks led by Qatar and Pakistan to de-escalate regional tensions.

Diplomatic Tracks and the Backstage of the Upcoming Tehran Visit

Timeline of the Visit: Prime Minister al-Zaidi’s state visit to Tehran is officially scheduled for next Thursday, though Baghdad has expressed full readiness to move the date forward if regional developments demand it.

Iraqi Request for a Supreme Leader Meeting: The Iraqi delegation expressed a strong desire to leverage the special bilateral relationship between the two neighbors to make al-Zaidi the first foreign official to meet with Iran’s new Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei.

Iranian Refusal Based on Security Protocol: The Iranian source completely ruled out the possibility of such a meeting, confirming that the Iraqi delegation was officially notified of the decision. The refusal was attributed to strict Iranian security anxieties regarding the potential exposure of the new Supreme Leader’s secure location, given that he has remained completely out of public sight since the outbreak of the war on Iran last February. Tehran noted that the standard official protocols and security footprint required for hosting a foreign prime minister would pose an unacceptable security risk.

Alternative Intelligence Claims: In contrast to Tehran’s official justification, regional and Hebrew media outlets quoted an Israeli security source claiming that Mojtaba Khamenei is not actually inside Iranian territory. The intelligence source alleged that the strategic messages attributed to the Supreme Leader are entirely drafted by Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Commander Ahmed Vahidi.

On the domestic front in Tehran, former Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif is spearheading a political narrative that encourages the Iranian leadership to maintain its current stance and resist external pressures until the conclusion of the American elections. Zarif based his strategic view on recent communications he allegedly received from several U.S. Democratic politicians. According to his account, these American figures suggested that a potential electoral setback for Trump in November could push Congress to take decisive legislative action to halt the war.

Conversely, the governing domestic alliance uniting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf remains firmly committed to pursuing direct diplomatic understandings with Washington to end the crisis. The position of this moderate faction was recently reinforced following a directive issued by the Supreme Leader, which ordered an immediate halt to internal political public criticism of state officials.

This directive was translated into immediate action on the ground, as strict orders were handed down to hardline, ultra-conservative media outlets to completely cease their coordinated media campaigns against Pezeshkian and Qalibaf. The state warned that any violation of this freeze would result in severe regulatory and legal penalties, up to and including the permanent revocation of corporate media broadcasting licenses.

World.title: Iraq’s Integrity Commission arrests electricity official over 4.5B IQD cable theft
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Federal Integrity Commission announced on Sunday, July 19, 2026, the arrest of a senior official within the Baghdad Electricity Distribution Company for the embezzlement and illicit seizure of state-owned electrical infrastructure materials valued at nearly 4.5 billion Iraqi Dinars (IQD).

According to an official statement released by the commission, a specialized investigative and auditing task force was deployed directly to the Ministry of Electricity to audit regional inventory systems.

The investigation revealed that the head of the warehouses for the Rusafa distribution branch had illegally seized high-voltage electrical cables totaling 4,406,000,000 IQD in value. The commission noted that the primary suspect executed the embezzlement scheme in direct cooperation with two civilian vehicle owners who assisted in transporting the stolen state property out of the facility.

The arrest was carried out under a formal judicial warrant issued by the Judge of the Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Court, in accordance with the statutory provisions of Article 315 of the Iraqi Penal Code, which strictly penalizes the embezzlement of public funds by state employees.

A formal seizure record was legally documented, and the primary suspect was presented before the competent investigative judge, who subsequently ordered him to be remanded in custody pending further judicial proceedings.

Investigation Brief: Rusafa Grid Embezzlement Case

World.title: Influencer Andrew Tate and brother arrested in Miami
World.content:
Washington – Radical social media influencer Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan were on Sunday in custody in the US, officials said, as Britain seeks their extradition to face new charges of rape, sex trafficking and assault.

Karena Thomas, assistant chief constable of the UK’s Bedfordshire Police, said the pair had been detained \”pending ongoing legal proceedings.\”

The US Marshals Service confirmed the arrests.

US news outlet TMZ posted video of law enforcement officers placing the self-professed misogynist and his younger sibling in handcuffs and escorting them into waiting vehicles in Miami on Saturday.

Asked by an onlooker if he had something to say, Tristan Tate did not respond, the footage posted on X showed.

UK prosecutors, who are now due to seek the brothers’ extradition, said the arrests came after they brought forward 38 further charges against the pair.

The Tate brothers now face 59 charges in total — 42 against Andrew and 17 against Tristan, British authorities said on Sunday.

\”We have decided to prosecute Andrew and Tristan Tate for further offences including rape, arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation and offences relating to indecent images of a child,\” Malcolm McHaffie, head of the UK’s Crown Prosecution Service’s (CPS) Special Crime Division, said in a statement.

\”The CPS has requested the extradition of the Tates from the US,\” he said, adding that the latest charges stem from receipt of new evidence from Bedfordshire Police that brings the total number of alleged victims in the Tates case to seven.

Earlier this year, police in Hertfordshire, north of London, said they were reopening a probe into rape and sexual assault allegations made by women against Andrew Tate between 2014 and 2015.

They also face separate rape and human trafficking allegations brought by different women and investigated by Bedfordshire Police, which covers their hometown of Luton, also north of London.

\”There is no place for male violence against women and girls, and we will continue to work tirelessly to support victims and investigate all reports made to us,\” Bedfordshire Police’s Thomas added.

– ‘Face justice’ –

The Tate brothers are also accused of tax evasion and money laundering in the UK.

Their attorney, Joseph McBride, said in a press release that the brothers \”are innocent.\”

\”We are confident that once a competent judge sees the facts, and once the Department of Justice confronts this egregious abuse of its own authority, Andrew and Tristan Tate will walk free,\” McBride said.

The Tates are dual British-US citizens who have been avid supporters of US President Donald Trump.

Lawyer Matt Jury, of McCue Jury & Partners who represent four alleged British victims of Andrew Tate, said Tate was \”now facing the real prospect of extradition to the UK after years of public campaigning by the four British women I represent.

\”They have spent years fighting for action to be taken, and I now urge the authorities to ensure this case proceeds as quickly as possible.

\”Andrew and Tristan Tate are accused of some of the most serious offences, including multiple counts of rape and human trafficking. It is time they face justice,\” he was quoted by the PA news agency as saying.

In March 2025, the US state of Florida launched a criminal investigation against them. The status of that investigation is unclear.

Andrew Tate is one of the most prominent proponents of the so-called \”manosphere\” network of communities, many of them online, that focus on traditional masculinity, anti-feminism, and self-improvement.

He promotes his divisive views, often incorporating alpha-male and aggressively misogynistic themes, to millions on social media including 10.8 million followers on X.

In Romania, where they have been based in recent years, the Tates face allegations of trafficking minors, sexual intercourse with a minor and money laundering.

World.title: Iraqi dinar declines against US dollar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar declined on Sunday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly declined in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,520 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,526 Iraqi dinars on Sunday’s morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,525 Iraqi dinars and 1,515 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate dropped, fluctuating between 1,523 and 1,522.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: 14 killed, many missing as flash floods, landslides ravage J&K’s Poonch, Rajouri
World.content:
Poonch: Residents gather in the aftermath of torrential rain-triggered landslides and flash floods, at Dhara Sangla village of Surankote tehsil, in Poonch district, Jammu and Kashmir. At least 12 people were killed and several others missing as rains unleashed landslides and flash floods across the twin border districts of Poonch and Rajouri in the union territory on Sunday, causing widespread damage to public and private infrastructure including roads and houses, officials said. (PTI Photo)

JAMMU: Torrential rain unleashed flash floods and landslides in Pir Panjal region of J&Kâs Poonch and Rajouri districts Sunday, killing at least 14 people, leaving several missing and burying homes under walls of water, rock and mud that barrelled down mountain slopes. Officials said the toll could rise as rescuers searched for those trapped beneath debris.CM Omar Abdullah cut short his stay in New Delhi and flew to Jammu to oversee relief operations after heavy rain triggered widespread devastation in the two border districts. Police, Army, SDRF, civil administration and local volunteers fanned out across worst-hit Surankote, Haveli and Mandi in Poonch, while LG Manoj Sinha reviewed rescue efforts and directed immediate relief for affected families.Heavy rain disrupted traffic on strategic Jammu-Srinagar NH-44, prompting authorities to urge commuters to avoid vulnerable stretches. Annual Amarnath Yatra, which began July 3, and pilgrimages to Vaishno Devi shrine in Katra and Shiv Khori in Reasi were temporarily suspended after IMD forecast adverse weather for the next three days.Officials said Lower Murrah in Surankote suffered the heaviest loss, where eight members of a family were swept away.Two bodies had been found by evening while search teams continued to retrieve the remaining six. The dead included Noor Safia, 59; her sons Sajad Ahmed, 16, Haqnawaz Ahmed, 10, and Shahnawaz Ahmed, 10; Khalda Kouser, 25, and her 2-year-old son Sofian; Bano Bi, 60; and Mohammad Akram, 7.Four more died in Sangla village, while a fatality is also reported from nearby Sangalani. Nazia Kouser, 28, died in Noona Bandi, and four injured were shifted to Poonch district hospital.LG Sinha said he had spoken to senior officials and reviewed rescue operations. âAffected families have been moved to safety. All departments are on high alert,â he said. âI urge residents to stay calm and follow official updates. I am deeply saddened by the loss of lives in Rajouri and Poonch.âCM Abdullah expressed grief over the deaths, offered condolences to bereaved families and prayed for those injured. His office said he had remained in constant touch with local MLAs before flying to Jammu to personally monitor the situation.Former CM Ghulam Nabi Azad also condoled the loss of lives and widespread destruction.Rescue teams pulled three boys to safety near Peer Kho temple in Jammu after Tawi swelled suddenly. In Rajouri, Army, police and SDRF rescued two boys stranded in flooded Dhangri riverbank and nine others marooned in Thanamandi.Armyâs White Knight Corps said troops âbraving challenging flood conditions and swift water currentsâ rescued 11 civilians, including five children.Authorities sounded a flood alert across Jammu division after water levels surged in Chenab and other rivers. Gates of Salal hydroelectric project in Reasi remained open for a second day during reservoir flushing, sharply increasing discharge into Chenab. Police in neighbouring Ramban also issued an advisory after gates of Baglihar hydroelectric project were opened, sending river levels higher.

World.title: Net services remain suspended in J&K’s Doda 3 days after man’s death in police firing
World.content: JAMMU: Three days after a 30-year-old man was shot dead in police firing, triggering protests by locals, internet services continued to remain suspended across Doda district of J&K for the third consecutive day on Sunday, disrupting communication, online transactions and other services.Officials have not yet issued any statement regarding the restoration of internet services.Locals complained that students, remote workers and job seekers are struggling with the internet shutdown, besides tourists as they canât make online payments through apps.Sources claimed the internet speed on mobile and the broadband as well has also been restricted in Kishtwar amid the heightened security in the region.On July 16, a police team attempted to stop suspicious individuals in the Jai Valley area on suspicions of cattle smuggling. During the interception, a scuffle broke out and there was an alleged attempt to snatch an officerâs weapon, following which another member of the patrol party opened fire, killing 30-year-old Arif Hussain and injuring three other SOG personnel.Following the death of Arif, an autorickshaw driver, protests erupted in Bhaderwah town of Doda district and surrounding areas.According to police, initial probe has revealed no terrorist links.

World.title: Farooq Abdullah meets Wangchuk’s wife, wishes him good health
World.content:
SRINAGAR: NC president Farooq Abdullah on Sunday met fasting climate activist Sonam Wangchukâs wife Gitanjali J. Angmo, pledging support for her husband and the people of Ladakh.

âMay your husband get better. May he remain healthy and may his struggle be successful,â Farooq told Angmo at Delhiâs Safdarjung Hospital where he and other NC functionaries had gone to enquire about Wangchukâs health. Angmo thanked Farooq.

Farooq said he was not allowed to meet the activist who has been on hunger strike in support of Cockroach Janata Partyâs demands for education minister Dharmendra Pradhanâs resignation over NEET paper leaks.

World.title: 'Fabrications aimed at making bad performance': NTA warns of criminal action on AI, fake OMRs
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Acting swiftly on a wave of post-result complaints,

(NTA) has warned of strict action against fake claims after finding that several optical mark recognition (OMR) sheets submitted in support of

result grievances were fake or AI-generated - the first time the agency detecting AI-made OMRs being used to challenge results.

The complaints relate to the June 21 NEET-UG retest, held after the May test was cancelled over paper leak. NTA on Sunday warned that candidates submitting digitally-altered OMRs or scorecards could face cancellation of results, debarment from NTA-led exams and even criminal proceedings.

Some candidates and parents - few even joining Cockroach Janta Party's Jantar Mantar protest - have alleged mismatches between expected and declared scores.

The allegations, spreading rapidly on social media, are also being quickly picked up by opposition parties to attack NTA, which has already faced flak over the paper leak.

Faced with the challenge - which marks a technological twist to earlier disputes that involved forged documents, purportedly torn or damaged answer sheets, and allegedly fabricated scorecards - NTA warned candidates submitting digitally altered OMRs or scorecards could face action.





Officials said the fabrications appeared aimed at masking "not-so-good performances" - even though the effort cannot fetch a seat in a medical college, as admissions are made by the Medical Counselling Committee under Directorate General of Health Services and the respective state counselling authorities, on the basis of the merit list issued by NTA.

"NTA is closely monitoring and scrutinising all complaints.

In the wake of many OMR sheets submitted for scrutiny turning out to be fake/AI generated, students and parents are advised to submit only original OMRs for scrutiny. Any fake/AI generated OMR may invite legal action against the complainant," the agency said Saturday. Sources in the agency were furious over fabrications saying that they might taint those who have succeeded because of sheer merit.

Officials said complaints verified so far had not established any discrepancy in declared results. "If any discrepancy is found during the ongoing verification, corrective measures will be taken. The total number and nature of such cases will be shared once the exercise is completed and all grievances have been addressed," an official said. The disclosure will cover the number and nature of complaints examined, the cases in which documents were fabricated and whether any declared result required correction, they said.

World.title: Congress demands independent probe into donation chori
World.content: NEW DELHI: Leaders of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi Sunday shot off a letter to PM Narendra Modi demanding an independent probe into the Ram temple donation issue and warning that his govt's credibility depends on its swift action - putting the controversy high on the opposition's agenda for Parliament's monsoon session that may lead to confrontation with govt.Also, with Cockroach Janta Party and activist Sonam Wangchuk planned to march to Parliament Monday over paper leaks and to demand the resignation of the education minister, many opposition parties have supported the protest, and are likely to turn up at Jantar Mantar for the Parliament gherao.The twin issues, on which the opposition is seeking a discussion, are likely to dominate the first week of the session, with BJP in the crosshairs. Congress believes these controversies can hurt the governing party politically as they affect a large segment of Indian population and youth.Kharge and Rahul told Modi that he had announced the formation of Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Teerth Kshetra in Parliament, and its members appointed by Centre are closely associated with RSS, VHP and affiliates, while its "disgraced former general secretary" is "your close associate".They said in the letter,"Your silence now in the face of such a crime is unacceptable."The Congress duo said the findings of the independent probe and the trust's accounts should be made public so that every devotee knows how their offerings have been used.There is a consensus among opposition parties that govt should discuss the issue in Parliament, with SP's Dharmendra Yadav, RSP's NK Premachandran, CPI's Sandosh Kumar stressing the demand in the all-party meeting with govt.Ahead of the session, govt's decision to break up Wangchuk's hunger strike through police action has led to the opposition condemning the Modi govt. -

World.title: Stormy session ahead as opposition flags temple row, NEET, E20
World.content:
New Delhi: Opposition on Sunday pushed for discussion in Parliament over embezzlement of donations at Ram temple, NEET paper leak coupled with the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar, and the row over E20 petrol, signalling a tumultuous monsoon session from Monday, as govt cautioned its rivals that any disruption of the legislature is bound to cost them politically.

Amid indications that govt is unlikely to allow its rivals to raise in Parliament the theft of temple donations, parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju called for consultation instead of a âmy way or highwayâ attitude over the issues to be picked up for debate.

âCongress has every right to raise its demand, but it canât force govt,â he said, after Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge wrote to PM Modi, timing their demand for probe and accountability with the sessionâs start, as several opposition MPs, including SPâs Dharmendra Yadav, raised the issue in an all-party meet led by defence minister Rajnath Singh and attended by 58 MPs of 40 parties.

Govt lists 8-bill agenda, silent on delimitation, women's quota





While listing its agenda of eight bills, govt made no mention of its likely move to revive the constitution amendment bill for raising the strength of Lok Sabha and rolling out one-third reservation for women from 2029.

Rijiju, though, told reporters later that govt could bring a new item in accordance with the rules after discussing it in the business advisory committee (BAC) during the session, a common practice.





He said people had seen that political parties that disrupt Parliament and do not allow discussion end up paying a price, an apparent reminder to BJP's rivals of their poor show in a string of assembly polls, with once-formidable regional parties Trinamool Congress and DMK losing in West Bengal and Tamil Nadu, respectively.

With several opposition members raising the NEET-UG paper leak and questioning govt for not engaging with protesters at Jantar Mantar, RSP MP N K Premachandran pushed for a structured debate over the issue, saying paper leaks affect students in huge numbers.

As some opposition MPs spoke of the recent fuel price hike, BJP ally and JDU MP Sanjay Jha sought a debate on the West Asia crisis as he credited govt for its energy management, saying it had ensured minimal rise in oil and gas prices compared with other countries and expanded supply for India through alternative sources. India had no role in the crisis, but it handled its adverse impacts deftly, he said.

At a BAC meeting later, Speaker Om Birla appealed to all parties for cooperation in ensuring smooth and orderly conduct of the proceedings.

World.title: Minister Manohar Lal dismantles Central Public Works Department’s ‘Delhi Club’
World.content:
NEW DELHI: For a long time, a group of officials belonging to

(CPWD) have attracted both envy and admiration for something they seem to possess in abundance â their tenacious rootedness while holding transferable jobs.

Housing and urban affairs minister Manohar Lal, however, revealed the secret of how they transformed into permanent fixtures, saying, âEver since we rolled out a transparent transfer policy, I have been approached by many, including some influential people, to get the transfers rescinded.â

Speaking at CPWDâs foundation day celebrations recently, the minister said, âI was told there were some people who never got transferred for 20-30 years.

No one was able to move them out. Big and influential people started approaching me for them when transfer orders were issued, saying they have known such employees for years. I told them that it would happen this time and we would see next year.â

Lal was referring to one of the most commonly known secrets of the city â the knack of CPWD employees in winning over Lutyensâ influentials who become dependent on them for their comforts, resulting in an equilibrium of convenience that few would like disrupted.





The minister said employees should think of what would benefit all their colleagues and not just themselves. He also urged CPWD staff to put in their best efforts to achieve public good.

Lal said as CM of Haryana, he had introduced a transfer policy for teachers in 2015 . He recalled that during former CM Chaudhary Bansi Lalâs tenure, when all ministers had offices on the fourth floor of the state secretariat, the education ministerâs room would be full during âtransfer seasonâ.

âI had suggested to the then CM and the education minister in 1996-97 that they should have a transfer policy. Some people paid heed to my suggestion, but said if it was done, people would be unhappy. They said no one would approach influential people with requests for transfers. Aur agar koi political aadmi ke dwar par koi aadmi nehin aayega toh usko roti kaise hazam hogi (If none will approach political leaders for transfers, how would they survive),â he said.

Lal said after the introduction of the transfer policy, people are happy as they donât depend on anyoneâs mercy. The transfers were done in accordance with criteria that had been laid down and a survey showed 93% of teachers were satisfied, the minister added.

World.title: Opposition protests invite to TMC rebels to all-party meeting
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In solidarity with the Mamata Banerjee-headed Trinamool Congress, opposition parties on Sunday staged a rare walkout from the all-party meeting to protest the govtâs invite to its breakaway faction, even as both warring groups took potshots at one another, foretelling a fiery session of Parliament from Monday.

Govt, however, defended its decision, asserting that it cannot deny space to the faction of 20 MPs who have approached Speaker Om Birla for recognising their merger with Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) and have already been allotted separate seats in Lok Sabha.

âIt is govtâs duty to invite every group,â parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju told reporters. Playing down the walkout, he said it was only for a brief period as opposition parties rejoined the meeting soon.

Facing disintegration and an existential crisis, TMC has leaned on other opposition parties, including Congress, which used to get short shrift from the party in Parliament when Mamata was West Bengalâs chief minister, to strengthen its cause.

John Brittas of CPM, which has been a bitter critic of Mamata, said they supported the party in the walkout in the interests of parliamentary democracy which is under âattackâ from BJP.





As Mahua Moitra, who is among the eight Lok Sabha MPs siding with Mamata, called the majority bloc of 20 MPs âtraitorsâ and demanded their disqualification, Sudip Bandyopadhyay, the chosen leader of breakaway faction, retorted that a âsmallâ party with only eight MPs no longer deserves front row seating in House.

Mahua was joined by members of other opposition parties as she slammed the invitation to Sudip as the NCPI leader and to Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar as its chief whip and claimed that they cannot be recognised under anti-defection law. Only original party can merge with another party, she added.

World.title: CJP protest in Delhi LIVE: Will end fasting today if government takes accountability for failures in education system, says Sonam Wangchuk
World.content:
Ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s proposed march to Parliament on Monday (July 20, 2026) to press for education reforms, climate and education activist Sonam Wangchuk said that he will end his hunger strike on Monday (July 20, 2026) if the government is ready to take accountability for failures in the education system or the MPs are ready to take up the issue in the parliament.

Many political leaders, actors and common people thronged the protest site at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, even as authorities put in place elaborate security arrangements and said that no permission had been sought for any such procession.

Also read: Neha, a prominent face of the CJP protests, presses on with hunger strike

Meanwhile, no permission has been granted for the march planned by the CJP to Parliament on Monday (July 20, 2026), when both houses will convene for the Monsoon Session, potentially setting up a showdown between the massive crowd and the heavy security arrangements expected to meet them in the morning. Security personnel with riot guns have been deployed in the national capital, prompting the CJP to issue a call for more people to arrive at the site.

The CJP’s 1.5-kilometre march is planned to start from the Jantar Mantar protest site at 9 a.m., before moving through the Patel Chowk roundabout and terminating at the new Parliament building.

World.title: Crowd swell at CJP protest site ahead of Parliament march
World.content:
On Sunday (July 19, 2026) afternoon, thousands of people were flowing through both entries to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest site at Jantar Mantar in central Delhi. With thousands of people inside the protest area, it was almost impossible to walk without bumping into another person.

The crowd has seen a dramatic increase compared to the initial days of the protest, which started on June 20.

People who have been at the site for many days said that there has been a marked increase in the crowd after police forcefully removed activist Sonam Wangchuk from the protest site on Saturday (July 18, 2026) morning.

At any given time, there was a queue of people trying to enter the protest site at both entries. Once you enter, at multiple points, protestors doubled up as crowd managers, while some volunteers fanned for other people and other volunteers sprayed water from handheld sprays as people moved through queues.

Standing next to a table filled with medicines and masks, Abhishek Saha, an Ayurvedic doctor from Rohini in north Delhi, was busy giving ORS packets, tablets, and band-aids to people coming in with various issues at regular intervals.

“It was started by another doctor, who was from Maharashtra, and now I’m looking after it. People have donated all the medicines,” Mr. Saha said, adding that he was expressing his solidarity for a better education system.

The table acts as a makeshift clinic for the people visiting the protest and many living there for many days now.

There was heavy deployment of Rapido Action Force, Nagaland Armed Force and Delhi Police personnel. At least 10-11 buses were seen near both entry points. Crossing multiple layers of barricades protestors found themselves in a sea of people, with AISA, SFI, and other student organisation camps where students on hunger strike rested amid heat and humidity. Volunteers of Krantikari Yuva Sangathan (KYS) fanned the protesters who were seated, listening to the leaders on the dias. Several groups sang songs and raised placards demanding resignation of the Education Minister.

Pawan Kumar, 28, from Uttar Pradesh, and Shambu Dayal Meena, 31, from Rajasthan, said that they met at the protest site and have been fasting for the past six days.

“There is a lot of anger against the current government. They don’t respect the Constitution,” Mr. Meena, a tribal, said. “When the CJI said cockroaches, it felt bad because it felt like he was talking about me. I had been unemployed in the past,” he said.

Sitting next to them, Janeshwar, 32, said, referring to the trio, “Here, a Dalit, a tribal, and an OBC person are sitting together and protesting. Why? Because the government has closed down thousands of schools and it is our children that suffer. Not the children of the rich.”

Ravi, a student from Rai Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, said his brother had appeared for NEET this year. “Students work hard and give their everything to government exams only to realise they have been leaked. I cannot even imagine the state of parents who lost their children to these scams,” he said.

“ I am glad that so many people have turned up today,” said 60-year-old Vinod Kumar Mehra, a social worker from Gurgaon. “For the youth who want to change the country, hunger strike is the only option to express their rage and that is what they are doing,” he said.

People turned up not just to demand the resignation of the Union Education Minister. “It is a platform for us to express our discontentment with the government,” said Priya (name changed), an IT professional from Gurgaon.

“From something as basic as waterlogged conditions during the monsoon to embezzlement of donations at the Ram Temple at Ayodhya, how much and for how long are we supposed to suffer?” she added.

World.title: India advises citizens to postpone travel to Iran amid rising instability
World.content:
India on Sunday (July 19, 2026) advised its nationals to postpone travel to Iran until the security situation improves and urged those already in the country to consider leaving through available commercial flights amid rising instability and conflict.

In a revised travel advisory, the Indian Embassy in Tehran underlined that the "recent days have seen an increase in levels of instability and conflict in Iran", necessitating heightened caution for Indian nationals.

"Indian nationals intending to travel to Iran for any purpose should postpone travel for the time being, until the security environment improves," the mission said.

It advised Indians already in Iran to consider temporarily exiting the country using available flight options.

Those choosing to remain in Iran have been asked to exercise the "highest possible level of caution", the embassy said.

"They should carefully monitor the news to maintain full situational awareness, and should avoid locations seeing higher levels of military activity such as those along the southern coast of the country," it said.

The embassy also urged Indian nationals to comply with instructions issued by local authorities.

It asked all Indians in Iran who have not yet registered with the embassy to do so immediately and to regularly monitor the mission's website and social media handles for further updates.

The advisory comes amid renewed security concerns in Iran following an increase in regional tensions and military activity.

In the last few days, the U.S. has targeted bridges, water desalination plants and electrical facilities in Iran, while Tehran has hit U.S.-allied countries throughout West Asia.

India has, in the past, issued similar advisories during periods of heightened conflict in West Asia and has urged its nationals to remain in contact with the embassy for assistance.

The Indian mission has also shared emergency helpline numbers for citizens requiring assistance.

World.title: ‘There was no need for Govt. intervention’: Wangchuk’s wife Gitanjali on Delhi HC refusing interim relief on hospital transfer
World.content:
Soon after the Delhi High Court on Sunday (July 19, 2026) refused to interfere with activist Sonam Wangchuk’s treatment at Safdarjung Hospital, his wife Gitanjali Angmo said the petition was “wrongly interpreted” and questioned why the government, if it had to intervene, couldn’t do so “democratically with the family’s trust”.

On Saturday (July 1, 2026), Mr. Wangchuk was taken forcibly to Safdarjung Hospital by the Delhi Police on day 21 of his hunger strike.

His health is fine and there was no need for government intervention, his wife said, speaking to reporters after the hearing. “If a man is fasting - and today is his 22nd day - he has fasted 35 days in Ladakh. His health is fine. There was no need for government intervention”.

She said they would be appealing on Monday (July 20, 2026), “to rectify the errors in the order today”. Ms. Angmo said the family wanted to shift him to Medanta or any other private hospital of its choice.

Sonam Wangchuk hunger strike LIVE updates - July 19, 2026

Ms. Angmo asserted that Mr. Wangchuk should have free access to his doctors, adding that they went to the high court with the petition “that a free Indian citizen has the liberty to be treated where he wishes by doctors he’s comfortable with”. She said that a letter was submitted to the court prior to the hearing, but they are still awaiting a response.

“He [Mr. Wangchuk] should have free access. His doctors should meet him. So this is a larger question to answer, does a citizen not have the right to access care of his choice? And if the government intervenes, can’t they do so democratically with family’s trust?” Mr. Angmo asked.

Earlier in court, Justice Mini Pushkarna said no interim order was required at this stage on a petition by Ms. Angmo, seeking permission to shift him to a private facility. The petition will be heard next on July 24.

Thousands gather at Jantar Mantar ahead of CJP’s march to Parliament

“The high court has not allowed it because they said they’re worried about his health. We submitted that they can send their doctors wherever he’s being treated,” Ms. Angmo said.

In a special hearing, Justice Pushkarna said Safdarjung doctors were closely monitoring the fasting activist, and it could not be said that any force was being used against him in violation of his bodily integrity. The judge also said the government’s removal of Wangchuk from Jantar Mantar to Safdarjung Hospital cannot be called arbitrary.

Later, Ms. Angmo said that they wanted to shift Mr. Wangchuk to Medanta or any other hospital in the national capital. “This is fundamental right. We were exercising right of our comfort and choice. There’s a trust deficit in this country. People don’t trust government institutions.”

“Is India truly democratic and free? We asked the judge, the way police is roaming the floor and take all our belongings and his tablet... He’s not in detention like he was in the Jodhpur jail. He should have free access. His doctors should meet him,” she added.

On current status of Wangchuk in hospital

Ms. Angmo said the High Court did not allow the hospital transfer saying that they are worried about the activist’s health. “His physician has no access. There’s obstruction everywhere. We asked for a sample to get a 2.9 potassium reading from a different test centre..if 2.9 is so life threatening, then they should have given us the sample far earlier,” she said.

“For 20 days when we were checking [Wangchuk’s health] every day, I got reports constantly. But since we got here we aren’t getting reports. The court has noted our demand that we get reports immediately. We want to go to a hospital where he gets all these things,” she added.

Mr. Wangchuk is still continuing the fast, she said. “Sonam wanted that he wanted to continue the fast. They have been asking him to have fluids but he didn’t have. He’s having water.”

‘In Wangchuk’s absence, number of protesters will double’

“We know the government took him [Mr. Wangchuk] here [Safdarjung Hospital] because they were afraid that if he led a protest many people would come,” she said, asserting that “those numbers will double” in his absence.

Ms. Angmo urged people to join the proposes ‘Chalo Sansad’ march on Monday (July 20, 2026). “May everyone join the march. Education is the foundation for the country. If we want to be a vishwaguru especially.”

“In no developed country do people get an education based on their economic status. The demographic dividend we had a decade back of 50% people below age of 25...if we leveraged that we would have a generation of leaders,” she said.

Students have shown that Gen-Z protests peacefully: Angmo

Ahead of the planned protest march, Ms. Angmo conveyed Mr. Wangchuk’s message to the public. “Sonam’s message to everyone is that even in his absence we must go with double the enthusiasm and four times the numbers.”

“The way he has been advocating people to demonstrate peacefully, I’ll tell everyone two things: march peacefully and watch out for nefarious disruptive elements. They will try to colour the protest. But over the last 22 days students have shown that Gen Z protests peacefully,” she added.

World.title: Senior AAP leader Manish Sisodia to join march to Parliament on Monday
World.content:
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Sunday (July 19, 2026) alleged that activist Sonam Wangchuk has been illegally detained by the Central government to prevent him from joining the march to Parliament on Monday (July 20, 2026), called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).

Senior AAP leader Manish Sisodia along with many others joined the CJP’s protest on Sunday afternoon at Jantar Mantar here and said that he would also join the march to Parliament in support of the “education revolution”.

Also Read | ‘Wangchuk not alone’: At least 21 continue indefinite hunger strike

“Tomorrow, don’t come in support of any party. Whatever may be your party, even if you are from BJP, look at your child and think whether you want a good education system for your child,” Mr. Sisodia told the media.

AAP national spokesperson and MP Sanjay Singh said that he had submitted a notice to the Rajya Sabha Secretary-General seeking a discussion under Rule 267 on the NEET paper leak, on police action against peaceful protesters, and on the demands raised by Mr. Wangchuk, an education reform activist.

Follow the Jantar Mantar protest LIVE

The party also alleged problems with NEET (National Eligibility cum Entrance Test) re-examination, which was conducted after the paper leak.

Attacking Prime Minister Narendra Modi, AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal said in a post on X, “Major irregularities are now coming to light in the Re-NEET exam results as well. Where are the poor students supposed to go? Modi-ji, you cannot even conduct a single exam properly; how will you run the country? You have ruined the nation over the last 12 years.”

Thousands gather at Jantar Mantar ahead of CJP’s march to Parliament

Re-NEET exam के नतीजों में भी अब भारी गड़बड़ी सामने आ रही है। बेचारे बच्चे जाएँ तो जाएँ कहाँ?



मोदी जी, आपसे एक exam ठीक से नहीं हो रहा, आप देश क्या चलाओगे? 12 सालों में आपने देश का बेड़ा गर्क कर दिया है। pic.twitter.com/BVQc5CbgDO — Arvind Kejriwal (@ArvindKejriwal) July 19, 2026

Meanwhile, Delhi Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president Harsh Malhotra alleged that Mr. Wangchuk sat on the hunger strike on June 28 in a protest “sponsored” by the AAP, the Left, and the Congress over the alleged NEET paper leak, even though a re-examination was satisfactorily conducted on June 21. “This clearly shows that the objective of the hunger strike was not to raise students’ concerns but to create disruption from the streets to Parliament during the Monsoon Session,” he said.

Mr. Wangchuk, who was on the 21st day of his hunger strike demanding resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, was whisked away by the police and hospitalised on Saturday (July 19).

World.title: Thousands gather at Jantar Mantar ahead of CJP’s march to Parliament
World.content:
Thousands gathered at the Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on Sunday (July 19, 2026) ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)’s planned march to Parliament, demanding resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, even as the Delhi Police issued a prohibitory order against marches, demonstrations, and assemblies of five or more people except at the designated protest site with prior permission.

Jantar Mantar protest LIVE updates - July 19, 2026

The unprecedented turnout, which spilled over to the streets surrounding Jantar Mantar, comes a day after activist Sonam Wangchuk was abruptly picked up by police and hospitalised against his will at Safdarjung Hospital.

Meanwhile, no permission has been granted for the march planned by the CJP to Parliament on Monday (July 20), when both houses will convene for the Monsoon Session, potentially setting up a showdown between the massive crowd and the heavy security arrangements expected to meet them in the morning. Security personnel with riot guns have been deployed in the national capital, prompting the CJP to issue a call for more people to arrive at the site.

“Prohibitory order under Section 163 BNSS is in force in the New Delhi District. Accordingly, protest marches, processions, demonstrations and assemblies of five or more persons are strictly prohibited, except at the designated protest site at Jantar Mantar, with prior permission,” Delhi Police said in an advisory.

The CJP’s 1.5-kilometre march is planned to start from the Jantar Mantar protest site at 9 a.m., before moving through the Patel Chowk roundabout and terminating at the new Parliament building.

Gitanjali J. Angmo, wife of Mr. Wangchuk, declared at Jantar Mantar that the activist’s fast would end on Monday “only if political leaders met him and provided an assurance that education and accountability are made the main issue of the Monsoon Session”.She had earlier shared a handwritten note from Mr. Wangchuk, billing the march to Parliament as “India’s 2nd freedom movement”.

Mr. Wangchuk had taken sugarless oral rehydration salts, but continued to refuse intravenous vitamin or saline drips, additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma told the court. Ms. Angmo shared a handwritten note from Mr. Wangchuk, billing the march as “India’s 2nd freedom movement”. Later in the evening, Ms. Angmo declared at Jantar Mantar that Mr. Wangchuk’s fast would end on Monday “only if political leaders met him and provided an assurance that education and accountability are made the main issue of the Session”. Mr. Wangchuk had started the strike with the demand of Mr. Pradhan’s resignation.

Support marches

Large rallies with hundreds of people also took place in several parts of the country including Mumbai, Nagpur, Bengaluru, Nashik, and Jammu. The march in Mumbai was led by Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray. In Guwahati, the All Assam Students’ Union organised a candle-light protest across in support of Mr. Wangchuk.

Roopak Ikhe, a resident doctor at a government medical college in Bahraich district, Uttar Pradesh, was suspended for allegedly taking out a march in support Mr. Wangchuk. An inquiry committee has been formed to investigate the matter, Sanjay Khatri, the Principal of Maharaja Suheldeo Autonomous State Medical College, informed local media.

Over a dozen students and others on Sunday continued their own hunger strikes over the alleged irregularities in examinations. Abhijeet Dipke, CJP’s founder, finished two days of fasting that he started immediately after Mr. Wangchuk’s transfer. Earlier in the morning, protesters formed a human chain to prevent the CPI (ML) Liberation-affiliated All India Students’ Association (AISA)’s fasting members from being transferred to a hospital.

Several high-profile Opposition figures and celebrities arrived at Jantar Mantar on Sunday to register their support to the CJP’s protest. Former Delhi Deputy Chief Minister Manish Sisodia, Azad Samaj Party chief Chandrashekhar Azad, Trinamool Congress MP Kirti Azad, and Trinamool leader Mahua Moitra were among those who showed up throughout the day.

“That is youngsters, fighting for their rights at Jantar Mantar,” Actor Prakash Raj said in a video posted from the stage after arriving late in the afternoon. Actor Shabana Azmi met Mr. Dipke and the protesting AISA students. Actor Swara Bhasker also came to the protest and registered her support for the cause.

(With inputs from Rahul Karmakar and Mayank Kumar.)

World.title: Security up in Delhi ahead of Parliament session, CJP rally
World.content:
The Delhi Police on Sunday said the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) had not sought any permission for its proposed march to Parliament on July 20.

Owing to the enforcement of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (erstwhile Section 144 CrPC) that prohibits unlawful assembly of more than five persons, no protests, marches or demonstrations will be allowed in New Delhi district and Parliament Street subdivision, except at the designated Jantar Mantar protest site with prior permission.

Also read: Jantar Mantar protest updates on July 19, 2026

As per an order of the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Parliament Street Subdivision, the prohibitory orders were put in place on June 24 and will continue till August 22, 2026.

“In view of reports of a proposed march to Parliament by CJP on 20.07.2026 (Monday), Delhi Police hereby categorically clarifies that no permission has been sought or granted for any such protest march or procession,” said Sachin Sharma, Deputy Commissioner of Police (New Delhi).

Thousands gather at Jantar Mantar ahead of CJP’s march to Parliament

Ahead of the said march and with the Monsoon Session of Parliament commencing on Monday, the officials said strict security arrangements had been put in place to “ensure public safety, security of protectees, and the protection of vital government installations”.

“Any person violating the prohibitory orders shall be liable for prosecution under Section 223 BNS and other applicable provisions of law,” the DCP said.

“The Parliament Street sub-division is a busy area with heavy vehicular and pedestrian traffic, and that police have received reports indicating that unrestricted public meetings, processions and demonstrations are likely to obstruct traffic, endanger human safety and disturb public tranquillity. Exercising powers under Section 70(1)(b) of the Delhi Police Act, 1978, read with Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Parliament Street, has prohibited the holding of public meetings, assemblies of five or more persons, processions, demonstrations, picketing, dharnas, slogan-shouting and public speeches without prior written permission,” an order from the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Parliament Street Subdivision, said.

The order also prohibited carrying of firearms, banners, placards, lathis, spears, swords, sticks, brickbats, and similar objects.

Multi-layered barricades

By Sunday evening, as thousands of protesters turned up to the site, members of the Rapid Action Force, Nagaland Armed Police and the Delhi Police were seen at the entry points, secured with multi-layered barricades.

Elaborate preventive arrangements have been made to ensure law and order during the Parliament session, the officials said. “Preventive deployment will remain in place throughout the Parliament session,” police officers added.

Security has been strengthened around Jantar Mantar, Parliament Street, Central Vista, Connaught Place, Shankar Chowk and other key locations, while rapid response teams have been positioned to respond to any contingency. Several police vans, buses and ambulances could be seen at the protest site. Protesters were frequently being asked to manage the crowd at the site, to keep the emergency gates clear. Announcements of Section 163 enforcement were also being made.

World.title: Morning Digest: Spain wins World Cup with Ferran Torres’ goal; thousands gather at Jantar Mantar ahead of CJP’s march to Parliament
World.content:
Spain silences Argentina to win World Cup crown

Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute to lift Spain to their second World Cup title with a ​1-0 win over gutsy, 10-man Argentina in Sunday’s (July 20, 2026) final. Torres’ deserved winner came ‌16 years and eight days after Andres Iniesta ​also scored in extra time to lift the Spaniards ⁠to their first World Championship with a 1-0 victory over the Netherlands. It came on La Roja’s 20th shot of the contest against the defending ‌champions, who failed to manage any to that point and struggled to wrest possession away from their superior Iberian opponents.

Thousands gather at Jantar Mantar ahead of CJP’s march to Parliament

Thousands gathered at the Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on Sunday (July 19, 2026) ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)’s planned march to Parliament, demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, even as the Delhi Police issued a prohibitory order against marches, demonstrations, and assemblies of five or more people except at the designated protest site with prior permission.

DMK, TDP should uphold their legacy of ensuring fairness delimitation, says Congress

Invoking the role played by the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) in previous rounds of delimitation, Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh said the two parties should not fritter away their legacy of ensuring fairness in the delimitation process. Speaking to The Hindu ahead of the Monsoon Session of Parliament, Mr. Ramesh said continuing with the 1971 Census as the basis for the distribution of Lok Sabha seats is crucial to maintaining the federal balance. The Congress, he said, favours extending the freeze for another 25 years, until 2051.

Government to move Bill in Rajya Sabha today to make insult to Vande Mataram a criminal offence

The Centre will begin the Monsoon Session of Parliament on Monday (July 20, 2026) with a move to grant statutory protection to the National Song Vande Mataram., listing the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026. This legislation seeks to amend the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971. The existing law penalises acts of disrespect towards national symbols such as the National Flag, the Constitution, and the National Anthem with imprisonment of up to three years.

Supreme Court holds abuse is uncivil, but not obscene

The Supreme Court of India has reasoned in a judgment that the use of four-letter expletives and their variations may be “abusive, unpalatable or uncivil”, but does not qualify as ‘obscene’ in law. “Use of mere swear words, profanities and vulgar expletives, however distasteful or uncivil they may be, cannot be equated with obscenity... Words which are merely vulgar or abusive may evoke a feeling of disgust, revulsion or shock, but that by itself does not make them obscene in law,” the court said.

Will end fast if education accountability issue raised in Parliament Monsoon Session: Wife Gitanjali conveys Wangchuk’s message

Activist Sonam Wangchuk will call off his indefinite hunger strike if political leaders meet him at the Safdarjung Hospital and assure him that the issue of education accountability will be raised during the Monsoon Session of Parliament beginning Monday (July 20, 2026), his wife Gitanjali Angmo said on Sunday (July 19, 2026). Addressing protesters at the Jantar Mantar, where the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has been spearheading a movement against the alleged NEET paper leak, seeking education reforms, Ms. Angmo said Mr. Wangchuk has conveyed that he would end his fast provided there is a commitment from political parties to take up the issue in Parliament.

Maharashtra panel to study ST benefits after Christian conversion allegations

The State government has formed a 27-member committee of legislators from Scheduled Tribes to examine the legal framework for benefits available to ST individuals after religious conversion. The move follows allegations raised in the Assembly regarding Christian missionaries in Nandurbar district’s Navapur taluka. The decision originates from an attention notice (No. 1773) moved by Anupbhaiyya Agrawal and other members during the 2025 monsoon session of the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly. The notice stated that Christian religious leaders, missionaries, and their institutions in Navapur taluka were using inducements to compel tribals and non-tribals to convert.

South Africa says radioactive contamination at nuclear plant was minor

Recent radioactive contamination incidents at Africa’s only nuclear power plant were minor and posed no public danger, officials said on Sunday (July 19, 2026), reaffirming South Africa’s intention to scale up nuclear power generation. “Airborne radioactive contamination” was detected during scheduled maintenance work at the Koeberg nuclear plant, about 30 kilometres (20 miles) north of Cape Town, between June 30 and July 16, they told a press briefing.

Palestinians say Israeli settlers torch mosque, factory

Israeli settlers set fire overnight to a mosque in a village in the occupied West Bank, a Palestinian official said on Sunday (July 19, 2026), as an AFP journalist saw the structure’s entrance scorched and Hebrew graffiti sprayed on its walls. The incident came during a period of increased attacks against Palestinian communities by settlers in the Israeli-occupied West Bank since the start of the Gaza war in 2023.

U.K.’s Burnham drops digital ID scheme to prioritise cost of living, say allies

Britain’s next leader, Andy Burnham, will scrap government plans ​for a digital ID scheme when he takes office, signalling his intention ⁠to focus resources on kitchen-table issues such as the cost of living, his allies said. Dubbed the ‘King of the North’ for his work as the mayor of Greater Manchester in northwestern England, Burnham will replace Keir Starmer ‌as Prime Minister on Monday (July 20, 2026), when he says he will also unveil his cabinet team of top Ministers. Mr. Burnham’s office said one of his first moves would ‌be to ditch a plan for all employees to hold a digital identity document, a ‌scheme ⁠designed to tackle illegal migration but deemed a “fiasco” by a cross-party committee of ⁠lawmakers.v

World.title: Gill on mounting injury list: Players are not able to finish 2-3 matches here
World.content:
India captain Shubman Gill has expressed his concerns around the increasing injury concerns which severely dented the team’s opportunity to put out a full-strength squad in England. With Hardik Pandya already missing the ODIs, India hoped to test Nitish Kumar Reddy and Harshit Rana, but both end up missing the series with different injuries.

Right through the three-match ODI series that India lost, they missed players at critical junctures. Before the series began, Rana was ruled out. And from the squad that was originally named, even all-rounder Nitish ended up missing the series with injury. Then in the middle of the series, Washington Sundar picked up an injury and then KL Rahul and Bumrah too ended up missing a game each because of illness and knee injury. And Gill said it is a huge concern.

“Yes, absolutely. If you look at the squad the first score we announced, out of that, at least 5 players didn’t play this match. So, one player is injured, you have to play a different combination. Two players (missing), a different combination. I think after every match, if a player is missing, we are missing a few tricks. If you look at the World Cup, we have played 11 matches in a row, and the players are not able to finish 2-3 matches here. We are forced to play a different combination, which we don’t think we will have to play. So, looking at all that, it is a little worrying,” Gill said.



With Bumrah missing the final ODI, India ended up taking the field with only five bowling options and paid the price as except for Axar, all the seamers ended up having an off-day. Gill then elaborated what sort of place it put him as a captain.“One day before the match, if you get to know that a player is injured, then it is almost like you want to take a chance. If a player is 80% fit, you play with 5 bowlers, and if they come out with five bowlers, who will you play with? So, all those things are difficult to think about,” he said.

Speaking of the series outcome, Gill said they were planning to try different combinations, but admitted they were not able to overcome the crunch moments. “I think we have had a pretty decent series in both the matches that we have lost. We were there in the game for the majority of it. It almost feels like we are in the game for about 80% of the game. And then the crunch moments, the moments that dictate the game, that’s where we are missing the break. And in those moments, that’s where inexperienced players obviously go (missing). If you have an experienced bowling group, batting group, that helps you a lot. And I think we need to get a little bit smarter in assessing the conditions,” he said.

World.title: India once dominated the textile trade. It needs institutions to make a mark again
World.content:
Few industries have shaped India’s civilisation as profoundly as textiles. Long before modern concepts of global value chains emerged, textiles were already woven into India’s economic, cultural and commercial fabric. Archaeological excavations at Harappa and Mohenjodaro (dating back 4,500 years) have uncovered spindle whorls, needles and dyeing artefacts, among the earliest evidence of textiles. What began in the Indus valley was sustained through centuries of trade, innovation and craftsmanship.

For nearly two millennia, Indian fabrics clothed consumers across Asia and Europe. During the Mughal period, Bengal became the world’s premier centre for cotton textiles. Dhaka produced the legendary muslin prized by royalty across continents, while Murshidabad, famous for its silk and muslin, emerged as one of the 18th century’s wealthiest commercial centres. The economic significance of all this was immense. India accounted for one-fourth of global economic output in 1700, according to Angus Maddison. Then the Industrial Revolution happened, powered by James Hargreaves’ spinning jenny and other mechanised weaving technologies. These disruptive technologies changed the rules of the game, in this case competitiveness. Competitive advantage stopped being about artisanal skill and became about technology, productivity and economies of scale. India increasingly became a supplier of cotton to Lancashire mills and a market for manufactured textiles.



Independent India’s textile journey has been an effort to reverse this. India today possesses a fully integrated textile value chain, from cotton to spinning, weaving, processing, garment manufacturing and exports. The key catch is the employment intensity of the sector. Apparel alone generates 153 jobs for every Rs 1 crore invested, against 27 in automobiles and 14 in steel. Yet its share of global apparel exports has stagnated at around 3 per cent for over two decades even as Bangladesh’s rose from 2.2 per cent to 9 per cent, Vietnam’s from 1 per cent to 6 per cent. How does a civilisation that once clothed the world end up with 3 per cent of a $521 billion global apparel market?

This is the question our new book, Stitching India’s Apparel Export Strategy: From Farm to Foreign, released last week, sets out to answer. The book presents a comparative policy analysis of China, Bangladesh and Vietnam through five pillars of competitiveness: Scale and ecosystem, capital, labour and skilling, clusters and institutions, and market access and trade facilitation.

The lesson from China is one of an ecosystem approach: Vertically integrated clusters, concessional finance and the Sinosure model of export credit insurance and institutional governance that transformed China into the largest apparel exporter. Bangladesh leveraged Least Developed Country (LDC) preferences through readymade garment (RMG)-specific finance, back-to-back letters of credit, and export processing zones offering plug-and-play infrastructure and one-stop regulatory services. Vietnam aligned foreign investment, industrial parks and free trade agreements (FTAs) into one integrated strategy and industry-academia partnerships to attract global manufacturers. Each country followed a different path, but all created integrated ecosystems that enabled firms to compete at scale. Besides all these aspects, one that is very important but much less talked about is the issue of undervalued Chinese currency. Estimates by the IMF, the US Treasury (2026) and Goldman Sachs suggest the yuan has been undervalued by 16 to 30 per cent against the US dollar, acting as an implicit export subsidy.



To realise the government’s ambition of $100 billion in Textile and Apparel (T&A) exports by 2030, India must strengthen these fundamentals of competitiveness across the entire value chain. The first is scale and ecosystem development. The “missing middle” of mid-sized, export-ready firms capable of handling large, fast turnaround orders remains a constraint. Equally relevant is fibre mix. Global apparel trade is dominated by man-made fibre (MMF). India’s textile industry remains skewed towards cotton, with a 60:40 cotton-to-non-cotton fibre consumption ratio, in contrast to the global average of 25:75. This mismatch locks India out of the fastest-growing segments such as activewear, technical textiles and athleisure. The recent rationalisation of the inverted duty structure in the MMF segment must now be complemented by investment in MMF spinning and weaving. Second is capital. India’s real interest rates of 6.2 to 8.2 per cent remain significantly higher than those of China (3.1 per cent), Vietnam (around 1 per cent) and Bangladesh (negative real rates). Delays in Goods and Services Tax (GST) refunds and export incentive disbursals also constrain liquidity. Next is labour and skilling. India’s apparel sector is highly dependent on migrant labour, moving from Bihar, Odisha and Jharkhand into production clusters such as Bengaluru, Tiruppur, Surat etc. There is high attrition and absenteeism during the festival season, when assembly lines fall short. In our opinion, a more sustainable model is to move factories to where the cheap labour is. Pearl Global’s Muzaffarpur unit in Bihar is a step in that direction. The gains are multiple: Higher female labour participation, lower migration costs and a pathway for labour-surplus states like Bihar to accelerate manufacturing-led growth.

Finally, with the UK-CETA (Comprehensive Economic And Trade Agreement) and EU-FTA, India has achieved tariff parity with competitors such as Bangladesh and Vietnam. But competitiveness extends far beyond tariffs. India needs seamless end-to-end integration of trade processes so exporters can move goods, documents and approvals with minimal compliance costs, speed and predictability.

The reform agenda for India is clear: Build an ecosystem approach to competitiveness. PM-MITRA (PM Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel) parks, announced in 2021, embody this approach by integrating the five pillars of competitiveness — scale, infrastructure, finance, skills and market access — within a single institutional framework. Their timely implementation is critical if India is to seize the current window of opportunity in global apparel trade. Complemented by the export promotion mission and the integrated programme for the textiles, these reforms can reposition India as a scale-driven, digitally-enabled, sustainable and women-inclusive global sourcing hub. History tells us that India once clothed the world through craftsmanship. The future will depend on whether it can stitch together an ecosystem where firms, finance, institutions and supply chains move with the speed, scale and predictability that global value chains demand.

Gulati and Rao are distinguished professor and senior fellow, respectively, at ICRIER. Views are personal

World.title: Patents should not put cancer care out of reach
World.content:
On July 8, the World Health Organisation (WHO) released its Global Status Report on Cancer. The figures are staggering: An estimated 20.6 million new cancer cases and nearly 10 million deaths worldwide each year, that is, more than 26,000 lives lost each day. At current rates, the WHO predicts 35 million annual cases by 2050.

In addition to the scale of the disease, the report highlights an inherent inequity. A woman with breast cancer in a high-income country has an 87 per cent chance of surviving five years, compared to about 42 per cent in a low-income country, a gap that is less due to biology and more due to where she happens to live. While 68 to 94 per cent of wealthier countries have access to the top 20 priority cancer medicines, only 9 to 54 per cent of low- and lower-middle-income countries do.



India’s own numbers fit into this picture, albeit not comfortably. With an estimated 15.33 lakh new cases expected in 2024, a Rajya Sabha standing committee noted that roughly one in nine Indians faces a lifetime risk of cancer. The committee has also sought expert recommendations to improve the affordability of cancer care and expand access to diagnostics. According to GLOBOCAN 2022 data, breast cancer accounted for over 1.92 lakh new cases and over 98,000 deaths in India in 2022. More than half of these cases are detected at an advanced stage, making treatment more expensive and less effective. I’m writing this while undergoing cancer treatment myself. What has struck me is not the disease itself but the ordeal of surviving it: Waiting for an appointment, the anxiety, and the arithmetic every patient does, working out which drug she can afford, which treatment package is feasible, and how much her insurance might cover.
